fields.title: Numbers
fields.subtitle: Bemidbar, “In the wilderness”
fields.description: The fourth book of the Bible, called in Hebrew Bemidbar, “In the wilderness”, from its first verse, and in English Numbers, after the two counts of the people that frame it. Israel sets out from Sinai with the tribes camped around the tabernacle, the priestly blessing on their heads and the cloud going before them, and almost at once they begin to complain. Moses longs for all the LORD’s people to be prophets; twelve scouts come back from Canaan, ten of them feeling like grasshoppers, and the people refuse to go in; Korah rebels, Aaron’s staff blossoms, Moses strikes the rock, and a bronze snake is lifted up on a pole. Then the seer Balaam, hired to curse, can only bless and sees a star come out of Jacob, and a new generation stands at last on the plains of Moab. In the Open Word Bible, a new translation from the Hebrew given freely to the public domain, with an introduction to the book’s shape and meaning and a conclusion on where to read next.

qa.question: What is the book of Numbers?
qa.answer: The fourth book of the Bible and of the five books of Moses. Its Hebrew name, Bemidbar, means “In the wilderness”; its English name comes, through Latin, from the Greek translation and refers to the two censuses of the people in chapters 1 and 26. Its thirty-six chapters follow Israel from Mount Sinai to the plains of Moab, across the Jordan from Jericho, over some forty years: the generation that came out of Egypt refuses to enter the promised land and dies in the wilderness, and their children are counted and made ready to go in.

qa.question: Who wrote the book of Numbers?
qa.answer: Numbers does not name its author, though it says that Moses recorded the stages of the journey (33:2), and Jewish and Christian tradition has received it as one of the five books of Moses. Many scholars think it gathers old lists, laws and stories that reached their final form much later. Christians hold a range of views on how it was composed, while receiving it as Scripture; the New Testament reads its story as written down to warn and teach the church (1 Corinthians 10:11).

qa.question: Why did Israel wander in the wilderness for forty years?
qa.answer: Because at Kadesh, after twelve scouts had explored Canaan, the people believed the ten who said the land could not be taken and refused to go in, even proposing to choose a leader and return to Egypt (Numbers 13–14). God pardoned them at Moses’ prayer, but declared that the generation which had refused the land would not enter it. They would wander forty years, a year for each day the scouts were in the land, and only Caleb and Joshua, who had trusted God, would go in with the next generation. Hebrews 3:19 sums it up: “it was unbelief that kept them from entering.”

qa.question: What is the bronze snake in Numbers 21?
qa.answer: When the people spoke against God and Moses, fiery snakes came among them, and many died. When they confessed their sin, God told Moses to make a snake and set it on a pole, and whoever had been bitten and looked at it lived (Numbers 21:4–9). Centuries later, when the Israelites had been burning incense to it, King Hezekiah smashed it (2 Kings 18:4). Jesus took it as a picture of his own death: “Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, and in the same way the Son of Man must be lifted up” (John 3:14).

qa.question: Who was Balaam, and what is the star out of Jacob?
qa.answer: Balaam son of Beor was a famous seer from Aram whom Balak king of Moab hired to curse Israel (Numbers 22–24). On the way his donkey saw the angel of the LORD barring the road when he could not, and when he came to curse, he could speak only blessing. In his fourth oracle he says, “A star will march out of Jacob, and a scepter will rise from Israel” (24:17), words that Jews and Christians alike have read as a promise of the Messiah. The New Testament remembers Balaam less kindly, as a man who loved the pay he could get for doing wrong (2 Peter 2:15), and Numbers 31:16 says Israel’s sin at Peor came on his advice.

fields.title: Introduction
fields.body_html:
The Israelites set out when the LORD commanded and camped when the LORD commanded. They stayed in camp for as long as the cloud remained over the tabernacle.

— Numbers 9:18

Numbers is the story of the longest detour in the Bible. The journey from Sinai to the edge of the promised land should have taken weeks. It took forty years, and a whole generation died on the way. In Hebrew the book is called Bemidbar, “In the wilderness”, from its first verse, and that is where nearly all of it happens. The name we use comes, through Latin, from the ancient Greek translation, and refers to the two counts of the people that frame the book, in chapters 1 and 26.

The two names, put together, tell you what the book is about. The people are counted, ordered and ready; then they spend a lifetime in the wilderness. Numbers is a book about what God does with a people who are rescued but not yet home, who complain, rebel and lose their nerve, and whom he still will not abandon. That is why the New Testament turns to it so often. Every Christian lives in the wilderness between the exodus and the promised land.

Two generations

The simplest way to follow Numbers is by its two censuses. The first, at Sinai, counts the generation that came out of Egypt. Chapters 1–25 tell its story: the camp set in order, the journey begun, and then complaint after complaint, until at Kadesh the people refuse to enter the land and are sentenced to die in the wilderness. The second census, on the plains of Moab, counts their children. Chapters 26–36 belong to them, a generation standing on the border, receiving laws for life in the land.

The journey itself falls into three stages: at Sinai (1:1–10:10), from Sinai to Kadesh and the long years around it (10:11–20:13), and from Kadesh to the plains of Moab across the Jordan from Jericho (20:14–36:13). Stories and laws are woven together throughout, sometimes in ways that seem abrupt. But the laws are usually answers to the stories: after the people despair of ever entering the land, chapter 15 begins with instructions for “When you enter the land where you will live”.

The camp around the tent

The first ten chapters show Israel as God meant it to be. Every man of fighting age is counted, tribe by tribe. The tribes camp in a great square, three on each side, “all around the tent of meeting”, with the Levites closest to it. The Levites belong to God in place of Israel’s firstborn, whom he spared on the Passover night. Everything has its place, and at the centre is God.

Then come laws for keeping the camp pure, the vow of the Nazirite, who sets himself or herself apart for the LORD for a time, and the blessing that the priests are to speak over the people, still spoken in synagogues and churches around the world:

“May the LORD bless you and watch over you. May the LORD make his face shine toward you and show you favor. May the LORD lift up his face to look on you and grant you peace.”

— Numbers 6:24–26

“So they will put my name on the Israelites,” God says, “and I myself will bless them.” Chapter 9 describes the cloud over the tabernacle, rising and resting, and the people moving or staying as it moves or stays, “for as long as the cloud remained”. And in chapter 10 the cloud rises, the silver trumpets sound, and for the first time the people set out. Whenever the ark moved, Moses prayed, “Rise up, LORD! Let your enemies scatter.”

Complaining in the wilderness

Three days later the trouble begins. The people complain about their hardships, and fire breaks out at the edge of the camp. Then they crave meat, and look back to Egypt with a strangely selective memory: “We remember the fish we used to eat in Egypt at no cost, and the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions and the garlic.” They do not remember the whips. “There is nothing at all, and all we ever see is this manna!”

Moses, for his part, reaches the end of himself. “I cannot carry this whole people on my own. The load is too heavy for me.” God’s answer is to share his Spirit with seventy elders, and when two of them prophesy in the camp instead of at the tent, and Joshua wants them stopped, Moses gives one of the most generous answers in the Old Testament:

But Moses said to him, “Are you being jealous on my behalf? If only the LORD would put his Spirit on all his people and make every one of them a prophet!”

— Numbers 11:29

The wish was granted at Pentecost. Meanwhile, God sends the quail Moses doubted he could provide, with a question that echoes through Scripture: “Is the reach of the LORD too short?” Then even Moses’ own brother and sister turn against him, and God defends him. Moses, we are told, is the humblest man on earth, and the one to whom God speaks “mouth to mouth, openly and not in riddles”.

The scouts and the refusal

The turning point of the book comes in chapters 13–14. Twelve scouts, one from each tribe, explore Canaan for forty days. They bring back a cluster of grapes so large that two men carry it on a pole, and a report that the land “does flow with milk and honey”. But ten of them add that the people are giants and the cities fortified: “To ourselves we looked like grasshoppers, and that is how we looked to them.”

Only Caleb and Joshua speak up. “The shelter over them has been taken away, while the LORD is with us. So do not fear them!” The people talk of stoning them, and propose to choose a new leader and go back to Egypt. It is the exodus in reverse. God threatens to destroy them, and Moses prays again, quoting back to God the words God spoke at Sinai: “The LORD is slow to grow angry and rich in faithful love, forgiving wrongdoing and rebellion.” God answers, “I have pardoned them, as you asked.”

Pardoned, but not excused. The generation that refused the land will not enter it. They will wander for forty years, a year for every day the scouts spent in the land, until they have died in the wilderness, and their children, whom they said would be carried off as spoil, will go in instead. One man is singled out:

But my servant Caleb is different: there is another spirit in him, and he has followed me with all his heart. So I will bring him into the land that he entered, and his descendants will take possession of it.

— Numbers 14:24

The next morning the people change their minds and attack anyway, without the ark and without Moses, and they are routed. Faith that comes too late, on its own terms, is not the same as obedience.

Rebellion and the priesthood

Chapters 15–19 are full of challenges to the order God has set up. Korah the Levite and his allies accuse Moses and Aaron: “You claim too much! Every member of the congregation is holy.” The ground opens and swallows them. When the people blame Moses for their deaths, a plague breaks out, and Aaron runs into the middle of the crowd with incense to make atonement:

He took his stand between the dead and the living, and the plague was held back.

— Numbers 16:48

To settle the question of the priesthood, God has a staff from each tribe laid in the tent before the testimony, and the next morning Aaron’s has budded, blossomed and borne ripe almonds. Life from dead wood is God’s sign of whom he has chosen. The priests and Levites receive no land, because God himself is their share; to Aaron God says, “I am your portion and your inheritance among the Israelites.” And the ashes of a red heifer are prepared to cleanse those who have touched the dead, in a book where there is a great deal of death.

The waters of Meribah

Chapter 20 opens with Miriam’s death and closes with Aaron’s. Between them comes the saddest moment in Moses’ life. At Kadesh there is no water, and the people quarrel with him again. God tells Moses to speak to the rock. Instead Moses says, “Listen, you rebels! Are we to bring water out of this rock for you?” and strikes it twice. The water comes anyway; God does not let the people go thirsty for their leader’s anger. But the verdict follows:

But the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “You did not trust me, and so you failed to show my holiness before the Israelites. For that reason you will not be the ones to lead this assembly into the land I have given them.”

— Numbers 20:12

Readers have long asked why so severe a sentence fell on so faithful a servant. The text points to unbelief and to a failure to show God’s holiness before the people. Perhaps the point is that the greater the leader, the more his example matters. Either way, Moses will see the land only from a mountaintop.

The bronze snake

As the people travel around Edom they lose patience once more, and speak against God and against Moses. Fiery snakes come among them, and when they confess their sin, God gives a strange remedy:

The LORD said to Moses, “Make a fiery snake and put it up on a pole. Anyone who is bitten can look at it and live.” So Moses made a bronze snake and set it on the pole. Whenever a snake had bitten someone, and that person looked at the bronze snake, they lived.

— Numbers 21:8–9

The cure is not medicine but looking, a trust in God’s word that a bronze image on a pole can save. Centuries later the snake had itself become an idol, and King Hezekiah smashed it to pieces (2 Kings 18:4). But Jesus took it as a picture of himself: “Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, and in the same way the Son of Man must be lifted up, so that everyone who believes will have eternal life in him.”

Balaam: the blessing no one could curse

Now the story moves, unexpectedly, to the other side of the hill. Balak king of Moab is terrified of Israel and sends for Balaam, a famous seer from the east, to curse them. God tells Balaam not to go, then lets him go, and on the way sends an angel to block his path, whom Balaam’s donkey can see and he cannot. It is a comic scene with a serious point: the great seer is blinder than his donkey.

Three times Balak takes Balaam up to a height to curse Israel, and each time Balaam opens his mouth and blessing comes out. “How can I curse a people God has not cursed?” And in the second oracle:

God is not a human, who might lie, nor a mortal, who might change course. Would he say something and not do it? Would he speak and not make it happen?

— Numbers 23:19

Israel, camped on the plains below, knows nothing of any of this. While they sit in their tents, God is defending them on the heights. In the fourth oracle, which no one asked for, Balaam sees further still:

I see him, but not now; I look on him, but he is not near. A star will march out of Jacob, and a scepter will rise from Israel; he will crush the forehead of Moab and tear down all the people of Sheth.

— Numbers 24:17

Jewish and Christian readers have long heard in this star a promise of the Messiah, the king who would come from Jacob, and many have recalled it when they read of the star that led the magi to Bethlehem.

A new generation

The next chapter is a shock. What no curse could do, sin does. At Peor Israel’s men join the women of Moab in the worship of their gods, “on Balaam’s advice”, as chapter 31 later reveals, and a plague follows until Phinehas the priest acts. Then comes the second census, and its verdict:

Among them there was not one man of those enrolled by Moses and Aaron the priest when they enrolled the Israelites in the wilderness of Sinai. For the LORD had said of them, “They will certainly die in the wilderness.” Not one of them was left except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

— Numbers 26:64–65

The rest of the book looks forward. Five sisters, the daughters of Zelophehad, ask for their dead father’s share of the land, since he had no sons, and God answers, “The daughters of Zelophehad are right in what they say.” Moses asks God to appoint a leader after him, “so that the congregation of the LORD will not be like sheep with no shepherd”, and Joshua is commissioned. There are offerings for the festivals, laws on vows, a war with Midian, the eastern tribes settled with a warning that “your sin will catch up with you”, a list of the forty years’ stopping places, the borders of the land, and cities of refuge, where someone who has killed by accident can be safe.

How to read Numbers

Read the stories in order and let the laws interrupt them; the interruptions are part of the book’s meaning. Keep a map nearby, because the journey matters. And read it alongside the New Testament passages that read it for us: Paul in 1 Corinthians 10, who says “These events became examples for us”, and Hebrews 3–4, which takes up Psalm 95’s warning, “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts”.

Notice, too, how often the book shows Moses on his face before God, praying for the very people who want to stone him. Numbers is full of rebellion, but it is just as full of intercession, and of a God who answers it. Again and again the people deserve to be destroyed, and again and again they are carried on.

Christians have always found their own lives in this book. The church, too, has been brought out of slavery and is not yet home; it, too, is tempted to look back to Egypt, to grumble at the manna, to measure the giants instead of the promise. The wilderness in Numbers is a hard place, but it is also the place where God feeds his people every morning, guides them by day and night, and teaches them to trust him. The question it puts to every reader is the one Caleb answered: will you follow with all your heart?

Some things in Numbers are hard. The punishments are severe, and the war against Midian in chapter 31 troubles many readers. The book does not soften them, and Christians have wrestled with such passages in different ways; it helps to read them within the whole story of a God who is patient for forty years, and whose purpose, from the first chapter of Genesis, is blessing.

The numbers themselves raise questions. The census gives 603,550 men of fighting age, which would mean a people of two million or more. Some take the figures as they stand; others note that the Hebrew word for “thousand” can also mean a clan or military unit, which would make the numbers far smaller. The book says that Moses recorded the stages of the journey (33:2), and tradition has received it as one of the five books of Moses; many scholars think it gathers old lists, laws and stories that reached their final form later. Christians hold a range of views on these questions.

About this translation

The text in this edition is the Open Word Bible, a new translation made directly from the Hebrew and given freely to the public domain. It is printed here at its Balanced level, which aims to be accurate and to read naturally aloud. A few things are worth knowing before you begin.

“The LORD.” Where the Hebrew uses God’s personal name, the four letters often written Yahweh, this translation follows long Jewish and Christian custom and writes “the LORD”.

Numbers as numbers. The census totals are given as figures, as the Hebrew gives them: “The total number enrolled was 603,550.”

Chapter and verse. In a few places the Hebrew text numbers its verses differently from English Bibles: the Hebrew 17:1–15 is the English 16:36–50, and the Hebrew 30:1 is the English 29:40. This edition follows the English chapters, and all the references in this introduction use English numbering.

“Faithful love.” The Hebrew hesed, God’s covenant love, is “faithful love”, as in Moses’ prayer: “as befits the greatness of your faithful love”.

For the reasoning behind every sentence of the translation, with the Hebrew beside it, see the Open Word Bible itself at openwordbible.org.

fields.title: Numbers 1
fields.body_html:
A census of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai

1The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the tent of meeting, on the first day of the second month in the second year after the people of Israel came out of the land of Egypt. He said, 2“Take a census of the whole congregation of the Israelites by clans and by ancestral families, listing the names of every male one by one. 3You and Aaron are to enroll them by their divisions, all the men in Israel twenty years old and up, everyone who can go out to war. 4One man from each tribe is to be with you, each of them the head of his ancestral family. 5These are the names of the men who are to assist you: from Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur, 6from Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai, 7from Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab, 8from Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar, 9from Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon, 10from the descendants of Joseph: from Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud, and from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur, 11from Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni, 12from Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai, 13from Asher, Pagiel son of Ochran, 14from Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel, 15and from Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.” 16These were the men chosen from the congregation, the leaders of their ancestral tribes. They were the heads of the clans of Israel. 17Moses and Aaron took these men who had been named, 18and they gathered the whole congregation on the first day of the second month. The people registered their descent by clans and ancestral families, and the names of those twenty years old and up were listed one by one, 19just as the LORD had commanded Moses. So Moses enrolled them in the wilderness of Sinai.

The count, tribe by tribe

20The descendants of Reuben, Israel’s firstborn, were listed by their family lines, by clans and ancestral families. Every male twenty years old and up who could go out to war was counted by name, one by one. 21The number enrolled from the tribe of Reuben was 46,500.

22The descendants of Simeon were listed by their family lines, by clans and ancestral families. Every male twenty years old and up who could go out to war was enrolled by name, one by one. 23The number enrolled from the tribe of Simeon was 59,300.

24The descendants of Gad were listed by their family lines, by clans and ancestral families. Every man twenty years old and up who could go out to war was counted by name. 25The number enrolled from the tribe of Gad was 45,650.

26The descendants of Judah were listed by their family lines, by clans and ancestral families. Every man twenty years old and up who could go out to war was counted by name. 27The number enrolled from the tribe of Judah was 74,600.

28The descendants of Issachar were listed by their family lines, by clans and ancestral families. Every man twenty years old and up who could go out to war was counted by name. 29The number enrolled from the tribe of Issachar was 54,400.

30The descendants of Zebulun were listed by their family lines, by clans and ancestral families. Every man twenty years old and up who could go out to war was counted by name. 31The number enrolled from the tribe of Zebulun was 57,400.

32From the descendants of Joseph: the descendants of Ephraim were listed by their family lines, by clans and ancestral families. Every man twenty years old and up who could go out to war was counted by name. 33The number enrolled from the tribe of Ephraim was 40,500.

34The descendants of Manasseh were listed by their family lines, by clans and ancestral families. Every man twenty years old and up who could go out to war was counted by name. 35The number enrolled from the tribe of Manasseh was 32,200.

36The descendants of Benjamin were listed by their family lines, by clans and ancestral families. Every man twenty years old and up who could go out to war was counted by name. 37The number enrolled from the tribe of Benjamin was 35,400.

38The descendants of Dan were listed by their family lines, by clans and ancestral families. Every man twenty years old and up who could go out to war was counted by name. 39The number enrolled from the tribe of Dan was 62,700.

40The descendants of Asher were listed by their family lines, by clans and ancestral families. Every man twenty years old and up who could go out to war was counted by name. 41The number enrolled from the tribe of Asher was 41,500.

42The descendants of Naphtali were listed by their family lines, by clans and ancestral families. Every man twenty years old and up who could go out to war was counted by name. 43The number enrolled from the tribe of Naphtali was 53,400.

The total of those enrolled

44These are the men enrolled by Moses and Aaron and by the leaders of Israel, twelve men, each representing his ancestral family. 45So all the Israelites twenty years old and up, everyone in Israel who could go out to war, were enrolled by their ancestral families. 46The total number enrolled was 603,550. 47But the Levites were not enrolled along with the others by their ancestral tribe.

The Levites are not counted

48For the LORD had told Moses, 49“The one tribe you are not to enroll is Levi. Do not include them in the census of the Israelites. 50Instead, put the Levites in charge of the tabernacle of the testimony, all its furnishings and everything that belongs to it. They are to carry the tabernacle and all its furnishings, look after it, and camp around the tabernacle. 51Whenever the tabernacle is to move on, the Levites are to take it down, and whenever it is to be pitched, the Levites are to set it up. Any outsider who comes near it is to be put to death. 52The Israelites are to camp by their divisions, everyone in their own camp and under their own standard. 53But the Levites are to camp around the tabernacle of the testimony, so that no wrath falls on the congregation of the Israelites. The Levites are to keep guard over the tabernacle of the testimony.” 54The Israelites did everything the LORD had commanded Moses. That is exactly what they did.
fields.summary: In the wilderness of Sinai Moses counts the men of Israel old enough for war, tribe by tribe, 603,550 in all. The Levites are not counted, for they are to care for the tabernacle.

fields.title: Numbers 2
fields.body_html:
The camps of the tribes on the east

1The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said, 2“The Israelites are to camp with each group under its own standard, beside the emblems of their ancestral families. They are to camp all around the tent of meeting, at a distance from it. 3Those who camp on the east side, toward the sunrise, are to be the camp of Judah under its standard, by their divisions. The leader of the people of Judah is Nahshon son of Amminadab. 4His division numbers 74,600 men. 5Next to Judah the tribe of Issachar is to camp. The leader of the people of Issachar is Nethanel son of Zuar. 6His division numbers 54,400 men.

7Then comes the tribe of Zebulun. The leader of the people of Zebulun is Eliab son of Helon. 8His division numbers 57,400 men. 9The total counted in the camp of Judah is 186,400 men, by their divisions. They are to set out first.

The camps on the south

10On the south side is to be the camp of Reuben under its standard, by their divisions. The leader of the people of Reuben is Elizur son of Shedeur. 11His division numbers 46,500 men. 12Next to Reuben the tribe of Simeon is to camp. The leader of the people of Simeon is Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai. 13His division numbers 59,300 men. 14Then comes the tribe of Gad. The leader of the people of Gad is Eliasaph son of Reuel. 15His division numbers 45,650 men. 16The total counted in the camp of Reuben is 151,450 men, by their divisions. They are to set out second.

The tent of meeting in the middle of the camps

17Then the tent of meeting is to set out with the camp of the Levites in the middle of the camps. They are to set out in the same order as they camp, each in its own place, under their standards.

The camps on the west

18On the west side is to be the camp of Ephraim under its standard, by their divisions. The leader of the people of Ephraim is Elishama son of Ammihud. 19His division numbers 40,500 men. 20Next to Ephraim is to be the tribe of Manasseh. The leader of the people of Manasseh is Gamaliel son of Pedahzur. 21His division numbers 32,200 men. 22Then comes the tribe of Benjamin. The leader of the people of Benjamin is Abidan son of Gideoni. 23His division numbers 35,400 men. 24The total counted in the camp of Ephraim is 108,100 men, by their divisions. They are to set out third.

The camps on the north

25On the north side is to be the camp of Dan under its standard, by their divisions. The leader of the people of Dan is Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai. 26His division numbers 62,700 men. 27Next to Dan the tribe of Asher is to camp. The leader of the people of Asher is Pagiel son of Ochran. 28His division numbers 41,500 men. 29Then comes the tribe of Naphtali. The leader of the people of Naphtali is Ahira son of Enan. 30His division numbers 53,400 men. 31The total counted in the camp of Dan is 157,600 men. They are to set out last, under their standards.”

The total in all the camps

32These are the Israelites who were counted by their ancestral families. The total counted in all the camps, by their divisions, was 603,550 men. 33The Levites, however, were not counted among the other Israelites, as the LORD had commanded Moses. 34So the Israelites did everything the LORD had commanded Moses. That is how they camped under their standards, and that is how they set out, each by clan and by ancestral family.
fields.summary: The tribes camp in their places around the tent of meeting, three on each side under their banners.

fields.title: Numbers 3
fields.body_html:
The family line of Aaron and Moses

1This is the family line of Aaron and Moses at the time when the LORD spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai. 2These are the names of Aaron’s sons: Nadab the firstborn, and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. 3These were the names of Aaron’s sons, the anointed priests, who were ordained to serve as priests. 4But Nadab and Abihu died in the presence of the LORD when they offered an improper fire before the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai. They had no sons, so Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests in the lifetime of their father Aaron.

The Levites given to Aaron

5The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 6“Bring the tribe of Levi forward and present them to Aaron the priest to assist him. 7They are to carry out duties for him and for the whole congregation in front of the tent of meeting as they do the work of the tabernacle. 8They are to take care of all the furnishings of the tent of meeting and carry out the duties of the Israelites as they do the work of the tabernacle. 9Give the Levites to Aaron and his sons. From among the Israelites they are given entirely to him. 10Appoint Aaron and his sons to carry out their duties as priests. Any outsider who comes near is to be put to death.”

The Levites in place of the firstborn

11The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 12“Look, I myself have taken the Levites from among the Israelites in place of every firstborn, the first child born to each mother in Israel. The Levites belong to me. 13For every firstborn is mine. When I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I made holy to myself every firstborn in Israel, both human and animal. They are to be mine. I am the LORD.”

A census of the Levites

14The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai. He said, 15“Enroll the Levites by their ancestral families and their clans. Enroll every male one month old and up.” 16So Moses enrolled them at the command of the LORD, as he had been commanded. 17These were the names of Levi’s sons: Gershon, Kohath and Merari. 18The names of the sons of Gershon, by their clans, were Libni and Shimei. 19The sons of Kohath, by their clans, were Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel. 20The sons of Merari, by their clans, were Mahli and Mushi. These were the clans of the Levites by their ancestral families. 21From Gershon came the clan of the Libnites and the clan of the Shimeites. These were the Gershonite clans. 22The number of those enrolled, counting every male one month old and up, was 7,500. 23The Gershonite clans were to camp behind the tabernacle, on the west side. 24The leader of the ancestral family of the Gershonites was Eliasaph son of Lael. 25In the tent of meeting, the Gershonites were in charge of the tabernacle and the tent, its covering, the screen for the entrance of the tent of meeting, 26the hangings of the courtyard, the screen for the entrance of the courtyard that surrounds the tabernacle and the altar, and its cords. They did all the work connected with these things. 27From Kohath came the clan of the Amramites, the clan of the Izharites, the clan of the Hebronites and the clan of the Uzzielites. These were the Kohathite clans. 28Counting every male one month old and up, there were 8,600. They were responsible for the care of the holy place. 29The clans of the Kohathites were to camp on the south side of the tabernacle. 30The leader of the ancestral family of the Kohathite clans was Elizaphan son of Uzziel. 31They were in charge of the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the holy utensils used in the priests’ ministry, the screen, and all the work connected with these things. 32The chief leader of the Levites was Eleazar son of Aaron the priest. He oversaw those responsible for the care of the holy place. 33From Merari came the clan of the Mahlites and the clan of the Mushites. These were the Merarite clans. 34The number of those enrolled, counting every male one month old and up, was 6,200. 35The leader of the ancestral family of the Merarite clans was Zuriel son of Abihail. They were to camp on the north side of the tabernacle. 36The Merarites were appointed to take charge of the frames of the tabernacle, its bars, posts and bases, all its equipment and all the work connected with them, 37and the posts around the courtyard, with their bases, pegs and cords. 38Those who were to camp in front of the tabernacle on the east, in front of the tent of meeting toward the sunrise, were Moses, Aaron and his sons. They were to carry out the duties of the sanctuary on behalf of the Israelites. Any outsider who came near was to be put to death. 39All the Levites enrolled by Moses and Aaron at the command of the LORD, by their clans, every male one month old and up, numbered 22,000.

Redeeming the firstborn of Israel

40Then the LORD said to Moses, “Enroll every firstborn male among the Israelites who is one month old and up, and make a list of their names. 41Take the Levites for me — I am the LORD — in place of every firstborn among the Israelites, and take the livestock of the Levites in place of every firstborn among the livestock of the Israelites.” 42So Moses enrolled every firstborn among the Israelites, as the LORD had commanded him. 43The total of firstborn males one month old and up, enrolled by name, was 22,273.

44The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 45“Take the Levites in place of every firstborn among the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock. The Levites are to be mine. I am the LORD. 46To redeem the 273 firstborn of the Israelites who are more than the number of Levites, 47collect about 2 ounces of silver for each one, by the sanctuary standard. 48Give the money to Aaron and his sons as the redemption price of the extra firstborn.” 49So Moses collected the redemption money from those who were more than the number redeemed by the Levites. 50From the firstborn of the Israelites he collected about 34 pounds of silver by the sanctuary standard. 51Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons at the command of the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
fields.summary: The family line of Aaron and Moses is given, and the Levites are given to Aaron to serve the tabernacle in place of Israel’s firstborn. The Levites are counted, and the extra firstborn of Israel are redeemed.

fields.title: Numbers 4
fields.body_html:
The work of the Kohathites

1The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said, 2“Take a census of the Kohathites from among the Levites, by their clans and their ancestral families, 3all the men from thirty to fifty years old who can enter the service, to do the work at the tent of meeting. 4This is the service of the Kohathites at the tent of meeting: the most holy things. 5When the camp is about to set out, Aaron and his sons are to go in, take down the screening curtain and cover the ark of the testimony with it. 6Then they are to put a covering of fine leather over it, spread a cloth of solid blue on top, and put its poles in place. 7Over the table of the Presence they are to spread a blue cloth and set on it the dishes, the pans, the bowls and the jars for the drink offering. The regular bread is to stay on it. 8Over these they are to spread a scarlet cloth, cover that with a covering of fine leather, and put the table’s poles in place. 9They are to take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand for the light, with its lamps, its tongs, its fire pans and all the jars for the oil used in tending it. 10Then they are to put it and all its utensils in a covering of fine leather and set it on a carrying frame. 11Over the gold altar they are to spread a blue cloth, cover it with a covering of fine leather, and put its poles in place. 12They are to take all the utensils used for the service in the sanctuary, wrap them in a blue cloth, cover them with a covering of fine leather, and put them on a carrying frame. 13They are to clear the fat-soaked ashes from the altar and spread a purple cloth over it. 14Then they are to put on it all the utensils used in serving at it: the firepans, forks, shovels and basins, all the utensils of the altar. Over it they are to spread a covering of fine leather and put its poles in place. 15When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the holy things and all the holy utensils, as the camp is about to set out, then the Kohathites are to come and carry them. But they must not touch the holy things, or they will die. These are the things in the tent of meeting that the Kohathites are to carry. 16Eleazar son of Aaron the priest is to be in charge of the oil for the light, the fragrant incense, the regular grain offering and the anointing oil. He is to oversee the whole tabernacle and everything in it, the sanctuary and its utensils.”

Do not let the Kohathites be cut off

17The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said, 18“Do not let the tribe of the Kohathite clans be cut off from among the Levites. 19This is what you must do for them, so that they will live and not die when they come near the most holy things: Aaron and his sons are to go in and assign each man his task and what he is to carry. 20But the Kohathites must not go in to look at the holy things even for an instant, or they will die.”

The work of the Gershonites

21The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 22“Take a census of the Gershonites as well, by their ancestral families and their clans. 23Enroll all the men from thirty to fifty years old who come to serve in the company of workers at the tent of meeting. 24This is the service of the Gershonite clans, both their work and what they carry. 25They are to carry the curtains of the tabernacle and the tent of meeting, with its covering and the covering of fine leather that goes on top of it, the screen for the entrance of the tent of meeting, 26the hangings of the courtyard and the screen for the entrance of the courtyard gate, the courtyard that surrounds the tabernacle and the altar, with their cords and all the equipment for their service. They are to do all the work that has to be done with these things. 27All the service of the Gershonites, all that they carry and all their work, is to be done at the direction of Aaron and his sons. You are to assign them, as their duty, all that they are to carry. 28This is the service of the Gershonite clans at the tent of meeting. Their duties are to be under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.

The work of the Merarites

29As for the Merarites, enroll them by their clans and their ancestral families. 30Enroll all the men from thirty to fifty years old who enter the service to do the work of the tent of meeting. 31This is what they are responsible to carry as their part of the service at the tent of meeting: the frames of the tabernacle, its crossbars, its pillars and its bases, 32and the pillars around the courtyard with their bases, tent pegs and cords, with all their equipment and everything used in their service. Assign by name the items they are responsible to carry. 33This is the service of the Merarite clans, all their work at the tent of meeting, under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.” 34So Moses, Aaron and the leaders of the congregation enrolled the Kohathites by their clans and ancestral families, 35all the men from thirty to fifty years old who entered the service for work at the tent of meeting. 36Those enrolled, clan by clan, numbered 2,750. 37These were the men enrolled from the Kohathite clans, all who served at the tent of meeting. Moses and Aaron enrolled them at the command of the LORD given through Moses.

The Levites enrolled for the work

38The Gershonites enrolled by their clans and ancestral families, 39all the men from thirty to fifty years old who entered the service for work at the tent of meeting, 40numbered 2,630 by their clans and ancestral families. 41These were the men enrolled from the Gershonite clans, all who served at the tent of meeting. Moses and Aaron enrolled them at the command of the LORD. 42The Merarite clans enrolled by their clans and ancestral families, 43all the men from thirty to fifty years old who entered the service for work at the tent of meeting, 44numbered 3,200 by their clans. 45These were the men enrolled from the Merarite clans. Moses and Aaron enrolled them at the command of the LORD given through Moses. 46All the Levites whom Moses, Aaron and the leaders of Israel enrolled by their clans and ancestral families, 47all the men from thirty to fifty years old who came to do the work of serving and the work of carrying at the tent of meeting, 48numbered 8,580. 49At the command of the LORD through Moses they were enrolled and each man was assigned his work and what he was to carry. So they were enrolled, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
fields.summary: The duties of the Kohathites, Gershonites and Merarites in carrying the tabernacle are set out, and the Levites of serving age are counted.

fields.title: Numbers 5
fields.body_html:
Unclean people sent out of the camp

1The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 2“Command the Israelites to send out of the camp anyone who has a serious skin disease or a discharge, and anyone made unclean by a dead body. 3Whether male or female, you must send them out and put them outside the camp. Then they will not defile the camps of the people in whose midst I dwell.” 4The Israelites did so; they sent them outside the camp. As the LORD had told Moses, so the Israelites did.

Paying back a wrong done to another

5The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 6“Tell the Israelites: ‘When a man or a woman does any wrong to another person, thereby breaking faith with the LORD, and that person is guilty, 7they must confess their sin openly. The guilty person must pay back the full amount owed for the wrong, add a fifth to it, and hand it over to the one who was harmed. 8If the injured person has died and left no close relative to receive repayment, then what is repaid for the wrong goes to the LORD, which means to the priest. This is besides the ram of atonement, with which the priest makes atonement for the guilty one. 9Every contribution among all the holy gifts that the Israelites bring to the priest will belong to him. 10Each person’s holy gifts are their own to give, but whatever anyone gives to a priest belongs to that priest.’”

The law for cases of jealousy

11The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 12“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: ‘Suppose a man’s wife strays from him and breaks faith with him, 13and another man sleeps with her, but it is hidden from her husband; she has defiled herself in secret, there is no witness against her, and she was not caught, 14and a fit of jealousy comes over him and he becomes jealous of his wife, and she has in fact defiled herself; or if a fit of jealousy comes over him and he becomes jealous of his wife though she has not defiled herself, 15the man is to bring his wife to the priest. He must also bring the offering required for her, about 2 quarts of barley flour. He is not to pour oil on it or add frankincense, because it is a grain offering for jealousy, a grain offering of remembrance that calls guilt to mind. 16The priest is to bring her near and set her in front of the LORD. 17Then the priest is to put holy water in a clay pot, take some of the dust that lies on the tabernacle floor, and add it to the water. 18The priest is to set the woman before the LORD, let down her hair, and put the grain offering of remembrance, the grain offering for jealousy, into her hands. In his own hand the priest is to hold the bitter water that carries the curse. 19Then the priest is to put her under oath and say to her, “If no man but your husband has slept with you, and you have not turned aside to uncleanness while you are bound to him, you will be free from the harm of this bitter water that carries the curse. 20But if you have turned aside while bound to your husband, if you have defiled yourself and someone besides your husband has slept with you —“ 21then the priest is to make the woman swear the oath of the curse, and he is to say to her, “May the LORD make you a byword in curses and oaths among your people, when the LORD makes your thigh waste away and your belly swell. 22May this water that carries the curse go inside you, to make your belly swell and your thigh waste away.” And the woman is to say, “Amen, amen.” 23The priest is to write these curses in a scroll and then rinse the writing off into the bitter water. 24He is to have the woman drink the bitter water that carries the curse, and this water will go into her and bring bitter pain. 25From the woman’s hand the priest is to take the grain offering for jealousy. He is to wave the offering before the LORD and present it at the altar. 26Then the priest is to scoop up a handful of the grain offering, its memorial portion, and burn it on the altar, and only then make the woman drink the water. 27Once she has drunk the water, if she has in fact defiled herself and broken faith with her husband, the water that carries the curse will go into her and bring bitter pain. Her belly will swell, her thigh will waste away, and her name will become a curse among her people. 28But if the woman has not defiled herself and is clean, she will be cleared, and she will conceive children. 29This is the law for cases of jealousy, when a wife who is bound to her husband turns aside and defiles herself, 30or when a fit of jealousy comes over a man and he becomes jealous of his wife. He is to have the woman stand before the LORD, and the priest is to do for her everything this law requires. 31The husband will be clear of guilt, but the woman herself must bear her guilt.’”
fields.summary: Unclean people are sent out of the camp, and a wrong done to another is paid back with a fifth more. A ritual is given for a husband who suspects his wife of unfaithfulness.

fields.title: Numbers 6
fields.body_html:
The vow of a Nazirite

1The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 2“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: ‘When a man or a woman makes a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite, to be set apart for the LORD, 3they are to keep away from wine and beer. They must not drink vinegar made from wine or from beer, and they must not drink any grape juice or eat grapes, whether fresh or dried. 4As long as they remain set apart, they must not eat anything that comes from the grapevine, not even the seeds or the skins. 5For the whole time of their vow of separation, no razor may touch their head. Until the time they have set apart for the LORD is complete, they are holy, and they must let the hair of their head grow long. 6Throughout the time they are set apart for the LORD, they must not go near a dead body. 7Even if their father or mother, brother or sister dies, they must not make themselves unclean for them, because the mark of their consecration to God is on their head. 8For the whole time of their separation they are holy to the LORD. 9If someone dies very suddenly beside them, and so their consecrated head becomes unclean, they must shave their head on the day of their cleansing. On the seventh day they must shave it. 10On the eighth day they must bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting. 11The priest is to offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and so make atonement for them, because they sinned through the dead body. That same day they must consecrate their head again. 12They must dedicate to the LORD the days of their separation once more and bring a year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. The earlier days do not count, because their separation was made unclean. 13This is the instruction for the Nazirite when the time of their separation is complete: they are to be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting. 14There they are to present their offering to the LORD: a year-old male lamb without defect for a burnt offering, a year-old ewe lamb without defect for a sin offering, a ram without defect for a peace offering, 15and a basket of bread made without yeast, loaves of fine flour mixed with oil and wafers spread with oil, together with the grain offerings and drink offerings that go with them. 16The priest is to present them before the LORD and offer the Nazirite’s sin offering and burnt offering. 17The ram is to be offered to the LORD as a peace offering, together with the basket of bread made without yeast, and the priest is also to present its grain offering and drink offering. 18Then at the entrance of the tent of meeting the Nazirite is to shave their consecrated head, take the hair, and put it on the fire under the peace offering. 19The priest is to take the boiled shoulder of the ram, one loaf and one wafer of bread made without yeast from the basket, and put them in the hands of the Nazirite after they have shaved off their consecrated hair. 20The priest is to wave them before the LORD as a wave offering. They are holy and belong to the priest, together with the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution. After that, the Nazirite may drink wine. 21This is the instruction for the Nazirite who makes a vow, for the offering they owe the LORD for their separation, besides anything more they can afford. They must do just what they promised in their vow, following the instruction for their separation.’”

Aaron’s blessing on the Israelites

22The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 23“Tell Aaron and his sons: ‘This is how you are to bless the Israelites. Say to them:

24“May the LORD bless you
and watch over you.

25May the LORD make his face shine toward you
and show you favor.

26May the LORD lift up his face to look on you
and grant you peace.”‘

27So they will put my name on the Israelites, and I myself will bless them.”
fields.summary: Rules are given for the vow of a Nazirite. Aaron and his sons are given the words with which they are to bless Israel.

fields.title: Numbers 7
fields.body_html:
Offerings for the dedication of the altar

1On the day Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, when he had anointed and consecrated it and all its furnishings, and had anointed and consecrated the altar and all its utensils, 2the leaders of Israel, the heads of their ancestral families, brought offerings. They were the leaders of the tribes, the men who had been in charge of those who were counted. 3They brought their offering before the LORD: six covered carts and twelve oxen, one cart for every two leaders and an ox from each one. They presented them in front of the tabernacle. 4The LORD said to Moses, 5“Accept these from them, so that they may be used for the work of the tent of meeting. Give them to the Levites, to each as his work requires.” 6So Moses took the carts and the oxen and gave them to the Levites. 7He gave two carts and four oxen to the Gershonites, as their work required. 8And he gave four carts and eight oxen to the Merarites, as their work required. They were under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest. 9But he gave none to the Kohathites, because they were responsible for the holy things, which they carried on their shoulders. 10The leaders also brought offerings for the dedication of the altar at the time it was anointed. They presented their offerings in front of the altar. 11And the LORD said to Moses, “They are to present their offerings for the dedication of the altar one leader each day.”

The offerings of the twelve leaders, day by day

12The one who presented his offering on the first day was Nahshon son of Amminadab, from the tribe of Judah. 13His offering was one silver dish weighing about 3 1/4 pounds and one silver basin weighing about 1 3/4 pounds by the sanctuary standard, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, 14one gold pan weighing about 4 ounces, full of incense, 15one young bull, one ram, and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering, 16one male goat for a sin offering, 17and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.

18On the second day Nethanel son of Zuar, the leader of Issachar, presented an offering. 19He presented as his offering one silver dish weighing about 3 1/4 pounds and one silver basin weighing about 1 3/4 pounds by the sanctuary standard, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, 20one gold pan weighing about 4 ounces, full of incense, 21one young bull, one ram, and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering, 22one male goat for a sin offering, 23and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Nethanel son of Zuar.

24On the third day it was the turn of Eliab son of Helon, the leader of the people of Zebulun. 25His offering was one silver dish weighing about 3 1/4 pounds and one silver basin weighing about 1 3/4 pounds by the sanctuary standard, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, 26one gold pan weighing about 4 ounces, full of incense, 27one young bull, one ram, and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering, 28one male goat for a sin offering, 29and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Eliab son of Helon.

30On the fourth day it was the turn of Elizur son of Shedeur, the leader of the people of Reuben. 31His offering was one silver dish weighing about 3 1/4 pounds and one silver basin weighing about 1 3/4 pounds by the sanctuary standard, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, 32one gold pan weighing about 4 ounces, full of incense, 33one young bull, one ram, and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering, 34one male goat for a sin offering, 35and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Elizur son of Shedeur.

36On the fifth day it was the turn of Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai, the leader of the people of Simeon. 37His offering was one silver dish weighing about 3 1/4 pounds and one silver basin weighing about 1 3/4 pounds by the sanctuary standard, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, 38one gold pan weighing about 4 ounces, full of incense, 39one young bull, one ram, and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering, 40one male goat for a sin offering, 41and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.

42On the sixth day it was the turn of Eliasaph son of Deuel, the leader of the people of Gad. 43His offering was one silver dish weighing about 3 1/4 pounds and one silver basin weighing about 1 3/4 pounds by the sanctuary standard, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, 44one gold pan weighing about 4 ounces, full of incense, 45one young bull, one ram, and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering, 46one male goat for a sin offering, 47and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Eliasaph son of Deuel.

48On the seventh day it was the turn of Elishama son of Ammihud, the leader of the people of Ephraim. 49His offering was one silver dish weighing about 3 1/4 pounds and one silver basin weighing about 1 3/4 pounds by the sanctuary standard, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, 50one gold pan weighing about 4 ounces, full of incense, 51one young bull, one ram, and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering, 52one male goat for a sin offering, 53and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Elishama son of Ammihud.

54On the eighth day it was the turn of Gamaliel son of Pedahzur, the leader of the people of Manasseh. 55His offering was one silver dish weighing about 3 1/4 pounds and one silver basin weighing about 1 3/4 pounds by the sanctuary standard, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, 56one gold pan weighing about 4 ounces, full of incense, 57one young bull, one ram, and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering, 58one male goat for a sin offering, 59and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.

60On the ninth day it was the turn of Abidan son of Gideoni, the leader of the people of Benjamin. 61His offering was one silver dish weighing about 3 1/4 pounds and one silver basin weighing about 1 3/4 pounds by the sanctuary standard, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, 62one gold pan weighing about 4 ounces, full of incense, 63one young bull, one ram, and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering, 64one male goat for a sin offering, 65and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Abidan son of Gideoni.

66On the tenth day it was the turn of Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai, the leader of the people of Dan. 67His offering was one silver dish weighing about 3 1/4 pounds and one silver basin weighing about 1 3/4 pounds by the sanctuary standard, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, 68one gold pan weighing about 4 ounces, full of incense, 69one young bull, one ram, and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering, 70one male goat for a sin offering, 71and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.

72On the eleventh day it was the turn of Pagiel son of Ochran, the leader of the people of Asher. 73His offering was one silver dish weighing about 3 1/4 pounds and one silver basin weighing about 1 3/4 pounds by the sanctuary standard, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, 74one gold pan weighing about 4 ounces, full of incense, 75one young bull, one ram, and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering, 76one male goat for a sin offering, 77and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Pagiel son of Ochran.

78On the twelfth day it was the turn of Ahira son of Enan, the leader of the people of Naphtali. 79His offering was one silver dish weighing about 3 1/4 pounds and one silver basin weighing about 1 3/4 pounds by the sanctuary standard, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, 80one gold pan weighing about 4 ounces, full of incense, 81one young bull, one ram, and one year-old male lamb for a burnt offering, 82one male goat for a sin offering, 83and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Ahira son of Enan.

The total of the leaders’ offerings

84This was the offering from the leaders of Israel for the dedication of the altar at the time it was anointed: twelve silver dishes, twelve silver basins and twelve gold pans, 85each silver dish weighing about 3 1/4 pounds and each basin about 1 3/4 pounds, so that the silver of all the vessels came to about 60 pounds by the sanctuary standard, 86and the twelve gold pans full of incense, each weighing about 4 ounces by the sanctuary standard, so that all the gold of the pans came to about 3 pounds. 87All the animals for the burnt offering were twelve bulls, twelve rams and twelve year-old male lambs, with their grain offering, and there were twelve male goats for a sin offering, 88and all the animals for the sacrifice of peace offerings were twenty-four bulls, sixty rams, sixty male goats and sixty year-old male lambs. This was the offering for the dedication of the altar after it was anointed. 89When Moses went into the tent of meeting to speak with him, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the mercy seat on the ark of the testimony, from between the two cherubim. And he spoke to him.
fields.summary: Over twelve days the leaders of the twelve tribes bring identical offerings for the dedication of the altar. Moses hears God speaking from above the ark.

fields.title: Numbers 8
fields.body_html:
Setting up the lamps

1The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 2“Speak to Aaron and tell him, ‘When you set up the lamps, the seven lamps are to shine out toward the front of the lampstand.’” 3Aaron carried this out, setting up its lamps toward the front of the lampstand, just as the LORD had commanded Moses. 4The lampstand was crafted like this: it was hammered work in gold, beaten out from its base to its blossoms. It was made in keeping with the pattern that the LORD had shown Moses.

The Levites are made clean and presented

5The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 6“Take the Levites from among the Israelites and make them clean. 7This is what you are to do to make them clean: sprinkle them with the water of purification. Then they are to pass a razor over their whole body, wash their clothes, and make themselves clean. 8They are to bring a young bull and the grain offering that goes with it, fine flour mixed with oil. You yourself are to take another young bull as a sin offering. 9Bring the Levites forward in front of the tent of meeting, and call together the whole congregation of the Israelites. 10When you have brought the Levites before the LORD, the Israelites are to place their hands on them. 11Aaron is to present the Levites before the LORD as a wave offering from the Israelites, so that they may do the work of serving the LORD. 12The Levites are to lay their hands on the heads of the bulls. Then offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to the LORD, to make atonement for the Levites. 13Set the Levites before Aaron and his sons, and present them to the LORD as a wave offering. 14By doing this you will set the Levites apart from among the Israelites, and the Levites will belong to me. 15After that the Levites may go in to serve at the tent of meeting, once you have made them clean and presented them as a wave offering. 16They are given over entirely to me from among the Israelites. I have taken them for myself in place of the firstborn, the first child born to every mother in Israel. 17For every firstborn among the Israelites belongs to me, of people and of animals alike. I made them holy to myself on the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt. 18So I have taken the Levites in place of every firstborn among the Israelites. 19I have handed over the Levites, taken from among the Israelites, to Aaron and his sons as a gift. They are to do the work of the Israelites at the tent of meeting and make atonement for them, so that the Israelites are not struck by a plague when they approach the sanctuary.” 20Moses, Aaron and the whole congregation of the Israelites carried out for the Levites all that the LORD had commanded Moses about them; the Israelites did exactly that with them. 21The Levites cleansed themselves of sin and washed their clothes, and Aaron presented them before the LORD as a wave offering. Aaron made atonement for them so that they would be clean. 22After that the Levites went in to do their work at the tent of meeting, serving under Aaron and his sons. What the LORD had commanded Moses about the Levites was done with them.

The ages of service for the Levites

23The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 24“This is the rule for the Levites: from the age of twenty-five and up, each one is to come and take his place on duty in the work of the tent of meeting. 25But from fifty years old he is to step down from the duty of the work and serve no more. 26He may help his fellow Levites at the tent of meeting by keeping guard, but he is not to do the work. This is how you are to arrange the duties of the Levites.”
fields.summary: Aaron sets up the lamps on the lampstand. The Levites are made clean and presented to serve, and their ages of service are fixed.

fields.title: Numbers 9
fields.body_html:
The Passover in the wilderness of Sinai

1In the second year after they came out of the land of Egypt, in its first month, the LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai and said, 2“The Israelites are to keep the Passover at its appointed time. 3On the fourteenth day of this month, at dusk, you are to keep it at its appointed time, following all its statutes and rulings.” 4So Moses told the Israelites to keep the Passover. 5They kept the Passover in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at dusk, in the wilderness of Sinai. Everything the LORD had commanded Moses, the Israelites did. 6But there were some men who were unclean from contact with a dead body, and so they could not keep the Passover on that day. That same day they came before Moses and Aaron. 7Those men said to him, “We are unclean because of a dead body. Must we be shut out, then, and not bring the offering of the LORD at its appointed time with the rest of the Israelites?” 8Moses said to them, “Stay here, and let me hear what the LORD will command for you.”

A Passover in the second month

9Then the LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 10“Tell the Israelites: ‘Any of you, now or in generations to come, who is unclean because of a dead body or is away on a distant journey may still keep a Passover for the LORD. 11In the second month, at dusk on the fourteenth day, they are to keep it, eating it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs. 12None of it is to be left over until morning, and no bone of it is to be broken. They are to keep it by every statute of the Passover. 13But anyone who is clean and is not on a journey, and yet holds back from keeping the Passover, is to be cut off from their people. They did not present the offering of the LORD at its appointed time, and they will bear the guilt of their sin. 14If a foreigner living among you wants to keep a Passover for the LORD, it must be kept by the statute and the ruling for the Passover. There is to be one statute for you all, for the foreigner and for the one born in the land.’”

The cloud over the tabernacle

15The day the tabernacle was set up, the cloud covered the tabernacle, the tent of the testimony, and from evening until morning it hung over the tabernacle with the look of fire. 16This went on all the time: the cloud covered it, and by night there was what looked like fire. 17Each time the cloud was lifted from over the tent, the Israelites would then set out, and at the place where the cloud came to rest, there they made their camp. 18The Israelites set out when the LORD commanded and camped when the LORD commanded. They stayed in camp for as long as the cloud remained over the tabernacle. 19If the cloud stayed on over the tabernacle for many days, the Israelites kept the charge of the LORD and did not move on. 20At times the cloud remained over the tabernacle for just a few days. They camped when the LORD commanded and set out when the LORD commanded. 21There were times when the cloud remained only from evening to morning; when it was lifted at daybreak, they moved on. Or if it remained a day and a night, they moved on when the cloud was lifted. 22Two days, a month or longer: however long the cloud lingered over the tabernacle, resting on it, the Israelites stayed in camp and did not move on; but once it was lifted, they moved on. 23They camped when the LORD commanded and set out when the LORD commanded. They kept the charge of the LORD, as the LORD commanded through Moses.
fields.summary: Israel keeps the Passover in the wilderness of Sinai, and those who are unclean may keep it in the second month. The cloud over the tabernacle tells the people when to set out and when to camp.

fields.title: Numbers 10
fields.body_html:
Two silver trumpets

1The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 2“Make two trumpets of hammered silver. You are to use them to call the congregation together and to set the camps moving. 3When they blow both trumpets, all the congregation must come together before you at the entrance of the tent of meeting. 4When a single trumpet is blown, the leaders, who head Israel’s clans, are to come to you. 5When you sound the alarm signal, the camps on the east side are to set out. 6When you sound the alarm signal a second time, the camps on the south side are to set out. The alarm signal is to be sounded whenever they set out. 7When you call the assembly together, give a blast on the trumpets, but do not sound the alarm signal. 8It is Aaron’s sons, the priests, who are to blow the trumpets. Their use is a lasting statute for you, generation after generation. 9In your own land, when you go out to war against an enemy who attacks you, sound the alarm on the trumpets, and the LORD your God will remember you, and you will be saved from your enemies. 10Also on your days of rejoicing, at your appointed feasts, and on the first day of each month, blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and over your peace offering sacrifices. They will be a reminder of you before your God. I am the LORD your God.”

Israel sets out from Sinai

11In the second year, on the twentieth day of the second month, the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle of the testimony. 12The Israelites set out from the wilderness of Sinai, traveling in stages, and the cloud came to rest in the wilderness of Paran. 13This was the first time they set out at the LORD’s command, given through Moses. 14The standard of the camp of Judah set out first, division by division, with Nahshon son of Amminadab in command of its forces. 15Nethanel son of Zuar was over the forces of the tribe of Issachar. 16Eliab son of Helon was over the forces of the tribe of Zebulun. 17Then the tabernacle was taken down, and the Gershonites and the Merarites set out carrying it.

18Next the standard of the camp of Reuben set out, division by division, with Elizur son of Shedeur in command of its forces. 19Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was over the forces of the tribe of Simeon. 20Eliasaph son of Deuel was over the forces of the tribe of Gad. 21Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things, and the tabernacle would be standing ready by the time they arrived.

22Next the standard of the camp of Ephraim set out, division by division, with Elishama son of Ammihud in command of its forces. 23Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was over the forces of the tribe of Manasseh. 24Abidan son of Gideoni was over the forces of the tribe of Benjamin.

25Last, the standard of the camp of Dan set out as the rear guard for all the camps, division by division, with Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai in command of its forces. 26Pagiel son of Ochran was over the forces of the tribe of Asher. 27Ahira son of Enan was over the forces of the tribe of Naphtali. 28Such was the order in which the Israelites marched by their divisions. Then they set out.

Moses asks Hobab to come with them

29Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law, “We are setting out for the place the LORD said he would give us. Come with us and we will be good to you, because the LORD has promised Israel good things.” 30But he answered him, “I will not go. I will return to my own country and my relatives.” 31Moses said, “Please do not leave us. You know the places where we can camp in the wilderness, and you will be eyes for us. 32If you go with us, then whatever good the LORD does for us, we will do the same for you.” 33They left the mountain of the LORD and marched three days, and all three days the ark of the covenant of the LORD went ahead of them, searching out a resting place for them. 34By day the cloud of the LORD was above them whenever they moved out from the camp.
35Whenever the ark set out, Moses would say,
“Rise up, LORD!
Let your enemies scatter,
and let those who hate you run from you.”
36And whenever it came to rest, he would say,
“Return, LORD,
to Israel’s thousands upon thousands.”
fields.summary: Moses makes two silver trumpets to call the people and signal the march. Israel sets out from Sinai, and Moses asks Hobab to come with them as a guide.

fields.title: Numbers 11
fields.body_html:
Fire at Taberah, and craving for meat

1Now the people began complaining about their hardships in the hearing of the LORD. When the LORD heard it, his anger flared up, and fire from the LORD broke out among them and burned up part of the outer edge of the camp. 2The people cried out to Moses, and Moses prayed to the LORD, and the fire died down. 3So that place was named Taberah, because the fire of the LORD had burned among them. 4The mixed crowd among them was seized by craving, and the Israelites began to weep again too. They said, “If only we had meat to eat! 5We remember the fish we used to eat in Egypt at no cost, and the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions and the garlic. 6But now we are wasting away. There is nothing at all, and all we ever see is this manna!” 7The manna was like coriander seed, and it looked like bdellium. 8The people went around gathering it. They ground it with millstones or crushed it in a mortar, then boiled it in a pot and made it into cakes. It tasted like pastry baked with olive oil. 9Whenever the dew settled on the camp at night, the manna came down with it. 10Moses heard the people weeping, family by family, everyone at the entrance of their tent. The LORD became very angry, and Moses was deeply troubled. 11Moses said to the LORD, “Why have you brought this trouble on your servant? Why do I find no favor with you, that you load me with the burden of this whole people? 12Was it I who conceived this whole people? Was it I who gave birth to them, so that you tell me, ‘Hold them close and carry them, as a guardian carries a nursing baby,’ all the way to the land you promised on oath to their ancestors? 13Where could I find meat for this whole people? They keep crying to me, ‘Give us meat to eat!’ 14I cannot carry this whole people on my own. The load is too heavy for me. 15If you are going to deal with me like this, then put me to death at once, if I have found favor with you, and spare me from seeing my own ruin.”

Seventy elders share the Spirit

16The LORD said to Moses, “Bring together for me seventy of Israel’s elders, men you know to be elders and officers among the people. Bring them to the tent of meeting and have them take their stand there with you. 17I will come down and speak with you there. I will take some of the Spirit that rests on you and place it on them. Then they will share the burden of the people with you, so that you will not have to carry it alone. 18And tell the people, ‘Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, and you will eat meat. You have wailed in the hearing of the LORD, “If only we had meat to eat! We were better off in Egypt!” So the LORD will give you meat, and you will eat it. 19You will eat it not for one day, or two days, or five, or ten, or twenty days, 20but for a full month, until it pours out of your noses and turns your stomachs. For you have rejected the LORD, who is among you, and you have wailed before him, “Why did we ever leave Egypt?”‘” 21But Moses said, “I am among a people of 600,000 men on foot, and yet you say, ‘I will give them meat, and they will eat it for a whole month!’ 22If flocks and herds were slaughtered for them, would they have enough? If all the fish in the sea were caught for them, would they have enough?”

Is the reach of the LORD too short?

23The LORD said to Moses, “Is the reach of the LORD too short? Now you will see whether my word comes about for you or not.” 24So Moses went out and told the people what the LORD had said. He gathered seventy men from the elders of the people and had them stand around the tent. 25Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to him. He took some of the Spirit that was on Moses and put it on the seventy elders. As soon as the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied, but they did not do so again. 26Two men, however, had stayed behind in the camp, one named Eldad and the other Medad. The Spirit rested on them too. They were among those listed, but they had not gone out to the tent, and they prophesied in the camp. 27A young man ran and told Moses, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp!” 28Joshua son of Nun, who had served as Moses’ assistant since he was young, spoke up: “My lord Moses, stop them!” 29But Moses said to him, “Are you being jealous on my behalf? If only the LORD would put his Spirit on all his people and make every one of them a prophet!” 30Then Moses and the elders of Israel went back to the camp. 31Then a wind went out from the LORD. It swept quail in from the sea and brought them down beside the camp, for about a day’s walk in one direction and a day’s walk in the other, all around the camp, about 3 feet above the ground. 32The people were up all that day, all night and all the next day gathering the quail. The one who gathered least gathered about 60 bushels. They spread them out for themselves all around the camp. 33While the meat was still between their teeth, before it had been chewed, the anger of the LORD flared up against the people, and the LORD struck them with a terrible plague. 34So that place was named Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had craved. 35From Kibroth-hattaavah the people moved on to Hazeroth, and they stayed at Hazeroth.
fields.summary: The people complain at Taberah and crave meat. Seventy elders share the Spirit, God sends quail, and a plague strikes those who craved it.

fields.title: Numbers 12
fields.body_html:
Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses

1Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses on account of the Cushite woman he had married, since he had married a Cushite woman. 2“Is it only through Moses that the LORD has spoken?” they said. “Has he not spoken through us too?” And the LORD heard it. 3Now Moses was exceedingly humble, more so than any other human being on earth.

4Without warning the LORD spoke to Moses, Aaron and Miriam: “You three, come out to the tent of meeting.” And the three went out. 5The LORD came down in a pillar of cloud and took his stand at the entrance of the tent. He called Aaron and Miriam, and the two of them came forward.
6Then he said, “Hear what I say:
