whenever you have a prophet,
I, the LORD, make myself known to him in a vision;
in a dream I speak with him.
7It is not so with my servant Moses;
he is trusted in all my household.
8I speak with him mouth to mouth, openly and not in riddles,
and he looks on the form of the LORD.
How is it, then, that you were not afraid
to speak against my servant Moses?”
9The anger of the LORD blazed against them, and he departed. 10As the cloud withdrew from above the tent, there was Miriam, stricken with a serious skin disease, like snow. Aaron turned toward Miriam, and there she was with the disease. 11Aaron said to Moses, “Please, my lord, do not make us bear the penalty for the sin we committed in our foolishness. 12Do not let her be like a child born dead, half its flesh already wasted when it leaves its mother’s womb.” 13So Moses cried out to the LORD, “O God, please heal her!”

Miriam shut outside the camp

14The LORD answered Moses, “If her father had merely spit in her face, would she not carry her shame for seven days? She must be shut outside the camp seven days; then she may be taken back in.” 15So Miriam was shut outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not break camp until she had been taken back in. 16After that the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.
fields.summary: Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses, and God defends Moses as the most faithful servant. Miriam is struck with a skin disease and shut outside the camp for seven days.

fields.title: Numbers 13
fields.body_html:
Men sent to scout out the land of Canaan

1Then the LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 2“Send men to scout out the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites. From each ancestral tribe send one man, and each of them is to be a leader among them.” 3So Moses sent them out from the wilderness of Paran, as the LORD had commanded. All of them were men who were heads among the Israelites. 4These are their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur. 5From the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori. 6From the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh. 7From the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph. 8From the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun. 9From the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu. 10From the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi. 11From the tribe of Joseph, that is, from the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Susi. 12From the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli. 13From the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael. 14From the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi. 15From the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi. 16These are the names of the men Moses sent to scout out the land. And Moses gave Hoshea son of Nun the name Joshua. 17When Moses sent them to scout out the land of Canaan, he told them, “Go up this way into the Negev, and go on up into the hill country, 18and see what the land is like, and whether the people who live in it are strong or weak, few or many, 19what kind of land they live in, whether it is good or bad, and what kind of towns they live in, whether they are open camps or fortified cities, 20and whether the soil is rich or poor, and whether there are trees in it or not. Be courageous, and bring back some of the fruit of the land.” It was the season of the first ripe grapes. 21So they went up and scouted out the land from the wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, near Lebo-hamath. 22They went up through the Negev and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai, the descendants of Anak, lived. (Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.) 23When they came to the Valley of Eshcol, they cut off a branch with a single cluster of grapes, and two of them carried it on a pole. They also took some of the pomegranates and figs. 24That place was called the Valley of Eshcol because of the cluster of grapes the Israelites cut there. 25After forty days they came back from scouting out the land. 26They came back to Moses and Aaron and the whole congregation of the Israelites at Kadesh in the wilderness of Paran. They gave their report to them and to the whole congregation, and showed them the fruit of the land. 27They gave Moses this account: “We went into the land you sent us to. It does flow with milk and honey, and here is its fruit. 28But the people living in the land are powerful, and the cities are fortified and very large. We even saw the descendants of Anak there. 29The Amalekites live in the land of the Negev. The Hittites, the Jebusites and the Amorites live in the hill country, and the Canaanites live by the sea and along the Jordan.” 30Then Caleb quieted the people in front of Moses and said, “We must go up and take possession of it, for we are surely strong enough to conquer it.” 31But the men who had gone up with him said, “We cannot attack these people, because they are too strong for us.” 32So they spread a bad report among the Israelites about the land they had scouted, saying, “The land we went through to scout out is a land that eats up those who live in it. All the people we saw there are men of huge size. 33We saw the Nephilim there, the sons of Anak, who come from the Nephilim. To ourselves we looked like grasshoppers, and that is how we looked to them.”
fields.summary: Moses sends twelve men to scout the land of Canaan. They bring back fruit and report a rich land with strong cities, and only Caleb urges the people to go up.

fields.title: Numbers 14
fields.body_html:
The people weep and rebel

1Then the whole congregation raised a loud cry, and the people wept that night. 2All the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole congregation said to them, “We wish we had died in the land of Egypt, or else died here in this wilderness! 3What is the LORD doing, bringing us into this land just so we can be killed in battle? Our wives and little ones will be carried off as spoil. Would going back to Egypt not be better for us?” 4And they said to one another, “Let us put someone at our head and go back to Egypt.” 5Then Moses and Aaron fell face down in front of the whole assembly of the congregation of the Israelites. 6Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, two of the men who had explored the land, tore their clothes. 7They said to the whole congregation of the Israelites, “The land we traveled through to explore is a good land, very good indeed. 8If the LORD takes delight in us, he will bring us into this land and give it to us, a land where milk and honey flow. 9Just do not rebel against the LORD. And as for you, have no fear of the people who live in the land; we will eat them up like bread. The shelter over them has been taken away, while the LORD is with us. So do not fear them!” 10But the whole congregation talked of stoning them. Then the glory of the LORD appeared at the tent of meeting to all the Israelites.

Moses pleads for the people

11The LORD said to Moses, “How long will this people scorn me? How long will they go on not believing in me, when I have done so many signs among them? 12I will strike them down with disease and take away their inheritance, and from you I will make a nation greater and mightier than they are.” 13But Moses said to the LORD, “Then the Egyptians will hear of it! It was by your power that you brought this people up out from among them, 14and they will tell it to those who live in this land. These have heard that you, the LORD, are present among this people; that you, the LORD, show yourself to them openly, eye to eye; that your cloud rests above them; and that you lead the way before them, in a pillar of cloud by day and in a pillar of fire by night. 15If you now kill this people all at once, the nations that have heard the report about you will say, 16‘It was because the LORD was unable to bring this people into the land he had sworn to give them that he butchered them in the wilderness.’ 17So now, I pray, let the power of my Lord be shown to be great, as you have declared: 18‘The LORD is slow to grow angry and rich in faithful love, forgiving wrongdoing and rebellion. Yet he will never acquit the guilty; he brings the wrongdoing of parents upon their children, to the third and the fourth generation.’ 19Please pardon the wrongdoing of this people, as befits the greatness of your faithful love, just as you have forgiven this people all the way from Egypt until now.” 20The LORD answered, “I have pardoned them, as you asked. 21Nevertheless, as surely as I live, and as surely as the glory of the LORD will fill the whole earth, 22all the men who saw my glory and the signs I did in Egypt and in the wilderness, and yet have put me to the test these ten times and have not listened to my voice, 23not one of them will see the land I swore to give their fathers; none of those who scorned me will see it. 24But my servant Caleb is different: there is another spirit in him, and he has followed me with all his heart. So I will bring him into the land that he entered, and his descendants will take possession of it. 25Now the Amalekites and the Canaanites live in the valley. Tomorrow turn around and set out into the wilderness along the road to the Red Sea.”

Forty years in the wilderness

26Then the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said, 27“How long must I put up with this evil congregation that keeps grumbling against me? I have heard the complaints the Israelites are making against me. 28Tell them, ‘As I live, declares the LORD, I will treat you just as you have spoken in my hearing: 29Here in this wilderness your bodies will fall, all of you who were enrolled, the whole number of you from twenty years old and upward, who have grumbled against me. 30You will certainly not enter the land that I raised my hand and swore to give you as a home, except for Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun. 31But your little ones, who you said would be carried off as spoil, I will bring in, and they will come to know the land you have rejected. 32But as for you, your bodies will fall in this wilderness. 33Your children will roam the wilderness as shepherds for forty years, bearing the burden of your unfaithfulness, until every one of your bodies has fallen in the wilderness. 34You spent forty days exploring the land; for each day you will bear your guilt for a year, forty years in all, and you will learn what my opposition means. 35I, the LORD, have spoken. I will surely do this to this whole evil congregation that has banded together against me: in this wilderness they will come to their end, and here they will die.’” 36As for the men Moses had sent to explore the land, who came back and made the whole congregation grumble against him by spreading a bad report about the land, 37those men who spread the evil report about the land died by a plague in the presence of the LORD. 38But Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh remained alive, the only two left of the men who had gone to explore the land. 39Moses reported these words to all the Israelites, and the people grieved deeply. 40They got up early in the morning and went up toward the heights of the hill country, saying, “Here we are! We will go up to the place the LORD spoke of, for we have sinned.” 41But Moses said, “Why are you doing this, going against what the LORD has commanded? It will not work. 42Do not go up, for the LORD is not in your midst; do not let your enemies strike you down. 43The Amalekites and the Canaanites are there ahead of you, and you will fall by the sword. Because you have turned away from following the LORD, the LORD will not be with you.” 44But they recklessly went on up toward the heights of the hill country, though neither the ark of the covenant of the LORD nor Moses left the camp. 45Then the Amalekites and Canaanites living in that hill country swept down on them, struck them and cut them to pieces as far as Hormah.
fields.summary: The people weep and rebel, wanting to return to Egypt, and Moses pleads for them. God forgives but says that generation will wander forty years and die in the wilderness, except Caleb and Joshua.

fields.title: Numbers 15
fields.body_html:
Grain and drink offerings with the sacrifices

1The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 2“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: ‘When you enter the land where you will live, the land I am giving you, 3and you present a food offering to the LORD from the herd or from the flock, a burnt offering or a sacrifice, whether to fulfill a vow, or as a freewill offering, or at your appointed festivals, to make a soothing aroma for the LORD, 4the one who brings the offering is to present to the LORD a grain offering of about 2 quarts of fine flour mixed with about a quart of oil. 5With the burnt offering or the sacrifice you are also to prepare about a quart of wine for the drink offering, for each lamb. 6For a ram, prepare a grain offering of about 4 quarts of fine flour mixed with about 1 1/4 quarts of oil. 7Also present about 1 1/4 quarts of wine for the drink offering, a soothing aroma to the LORD. 8When you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering, or as a sacrifice to fulfill a vow, or as a peace offering to the LORD, 9then with the young bull a grain offering is to be presented, about 6 quarts of fine flour mixed with about 2 quarts of oil. 10And present about 2 quarts of wine for the drink offering. It is a food offering, a soothing aroma to the LORD. 11This is what is to be done for each bull or ram, and for each lamb or young goat. 12However many animals you prepare, do this for each one of them. 13Everyone who is native-born is to do these things in this way when presenting a food offering, a soothing aroma to the LORD. 14If an outsider is living with you, or anyone else who is among you in generations to come, and presents a food offering, a soothing aroma to the LORD, they are to do it just as you do. 15For the assembly there is to be one statute for you and for the outsider who lives with you. It is a lasting statute through all your generations: before the LORD the outsider is to be just as you are. 16One law and one ruling are to apply to you and to the outsider who lives with you.’”

A loaf from the first of the dough

17The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 18“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: ‘When you come into the land where I am bringing you, 19then, when you eat the food that the land produces, you are to set aside a contribution for the LORD. 20From the first of your dough you are to set aside a loaf as a contribution. Set it aside just as you do the contribution from the threshing floor. 21Throughout your generations you are to give the LORD a contribution from the first of your dough.

Sins committed unintentionally

22Now suppose you go astray without meaning to and fail to keep all these commandments that the LORD spoke to Moses, 23everything that the LORD has commanded you through Moses, from the day the LORD first gave commands and on through your generations, 24if it was done unintentionally, without the congregation being aware of it, the whole congregation is to prepare one young bull as a burnt offering, a soothing aroma to the LORD, together with its grain offering and its drink offering as prescribed, and one male goat as a sin offering. 25The priest is to make atonement for the whole congregation of the Israelites, and they will be forgiven, because it was a mistake and they have brought their offering, a food offering to the LORD, and their sin offering before the LORD for their mistake. 26The whole congregation of the Israelites will be forgiven, and so will the outsider living among them, because the whole people was caught up in the mistake.

27When a single person sins unintentionally, that person is to bring a year-old female goat for a sin offering. 28The priest is to make atonement before the LORD for the one who went astray and sinned unintentionally. Once atonement is made, that person will be forgiven. 29Whether native-born among the Israelites or an outsider living among them, you are to have one law for anyone who does wrong unintentionally. 30But anyone who sins defiantly, whether native-born or outsider, insults the LORD, and that person must be cut off from among the people. 31That person has scorned what the LORD said and broken his commandment, and so must be cut off completely. The guilt rests on them.’”

A man collecting wood on the Sabbath

32Once, when the Israelites were in the wilderness, some of them came upon a man collecting wood on the Sabbath day. 33Those who caught him collecting wood brought him to Moses and Aaron and the whole congregation. 34They held him under guard, because it had not yet been made clear what was to be done with him.

35Then the LORD said to Moses, “The man must be put to death. The whole congregation is to stone him outside the camp.” 36So the whole congregation took him outside the camp and stoned him to death, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

Tassels on the corners of clothing

37The LORD said to Moses, 38“Speak to the Israelites. Tell them that in every generation they are to make tassels for the corners of their clothing and fasten a blue cord to the tassel at each corner. 39‘Whenever you see this tassel, it will remind you of all the commandments of the LORD, so that you do them and do not wander after your own heart and your own eyes, following them in unfaithfulness, 40so that you remember and do all my commandments and are holy to your God. 41I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD your God.’”
fields.summary: Instructions are given for grain and drink offerings, for a loaf from the first of the dough and for sins committed unintentionally. A man collecting wood on the Sabbath is put to death, and Israel is to wear tassels as a reminder of God’s commands.

fields.title: Numbers 16
fields.body_html:
Korah, Dathan and Abiram rebel

1Now Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, gathered men to his side, together with Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, who were Reubenites, 2and they rose up against Moses. With them were 250 men from among the Israelites, leaders of the congregation, chosen members of the council, men of renown. 3They came together against Moses and Aaron and said to them, “You claim too much! Every member of the congregation is holy, all of them, and the LORD is among them. What right have you to raise yourselves above the assembly of the LORD?” 4When Moses heard this, he fell facedown. 5Then he said to Korah and all his company, “In the morning the LORD will show who belongs to him and who is holy, and he will let that man come near to him. The one he chooses, he will bring near to himself. 6Do this, Korah, you and all your company: take censers, 7and tomorrow put fire in them and lay incense on them before the LORD. The man the LORD chooses will be the one who is holy. It is you Levites who claim too much!” 8Moses also said to Korah, “Listen, you Levites! 9Does it mean so little to you that the God of Israel has set you apart from the congregation of Israel, bringing you near to himself to do the work of the LORD’s tabernacle and to stand before the congregation and serve them? 10He has brought you near, you and all your fellow Levites with you, and now you want the priesthood as well? 11So it is against the LORD that you and all your company have banded together. Who is Aaron, that you grumble against him?” 12Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab. But they said, “We will not come up! 13Was it a small thing to bring us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey only to kill us in the wilderness? Must you now also lord it over us, and lord it completely? 14Besides, you have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey or given us fields and vineyards to own. Do you mean to gouge out the eyes of these men? We will not come up!” 15Moses was furious, and he said to the LORD, “Pay no regard to their offering. I have not taken so much as one donkey from them, and I have done none of them any wrong.” 16Moses said to Korah, “Tomorrow you and all your company must appear before the LORD: you, they, and Aaron. 17Each man is to take his censer and put incense on it, and each is to bring his censer before the LORD, 250 censers. You and Aaron are also to bring your censers.” 18So each man took his censer, put fire in it, and laid incense on it. Then they stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting with Moses and Aaron. 19Korah gathered the whole congregation against Moses and Aaron at the entrance of the tent of meeting. Then the glory of the LORD appeared to the whole congregation.

20The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said, 21“Get away from this congregation, so that I can destroy them in an instant.” 22But they fell facedown and said, “God, God of the spirits of all humankind, when one man sins, will you be angry with the whole congregation?”

The ground swallows the rebels

23The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 24“Tell the congregation, ‘Move away from around the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.’” 25Then Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel followed him. 26He told the congregation, “Move away now from the tents of these wicked men! Do not touch anything that belongs to them, or you will be swept away when they are punished for all their sins.” 27So the people moved away from all around the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Dathan and Abiram had come out and were standing at the entrances of their tents, together with their wives, their children, and their little ones. 28Then Moses said, “This is how you will know that the LORD sent me to do all these things, and that they were not my own idea. 29If these men die the way all people die, and only what comes to everyone comes to them, then the LORD has not sent me. 30But if the LORD does something entirely new, and the ground opens its mouth and swallows them along with everything they have, so that they go down alive into Sheol, then you will know that these men have treated the LORD with contempt.” 31The moment he finished saying all this, the ground beneath them split open. 32The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, together with their households, all Korah’s people, and all their possessions. 33They went down alive into Sheol, they and all that was theirs. The earth closed over them, and they perished, gone from among the assembly. 34All Israel around them fled at their cries, for they said, “The earth may swallow us too!” 35Then fire came out from the LORD and devoured the 250 men who were offering incense.

36Then the LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 37“Tell Eleazar son of Aaron the priest to take the censers out of the burned remains and to scatter the coals far and wide, because the censers are holy. 38These men sinned at the cost of their own lives. Have their censers hammered into thin sheets to cover the altar. They were presented before the LORD, and so they became holy. Let them be a sign to the Israelites.” 39So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers that had been presented by the men who were burned, and they were hammered out to cover the altar, 40as a reminder to the Israelites that no outsider, no one who is not a descendant of Aaron, should come near to burn incense before the LORD, or he would become like Korah and his company. This was done as the LORD had told Eleazar through Moses. 41The very next day the whole congregation of the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron. “You have killed the people of the LORD!” they said. 42But when the congregation gathered against Moses and Aaron and they turned toward the tent of meeting, they saw that the cloud covered it, and the glory of the LORD appeared.

The censers cover the altar

43Moses and Aaron came to the front of the tent of meeting,

44and the LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 45“Get away from this congregation, and I will wipe them out in a moment.” But they fell face down. 46Moses said to Aaron, “Take your censer, put fire in it from the altar, and lay incense on it. Then take it quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them, because wrath has gone out from the LORD. The plague has begun!” 47So Aaron took it as Moses had said and ran into the middle of the assembly. The plague had already begun among the people, but he put the incense on and made atonement for them. 48He took his stand between the dead and the living, and the plague was held back. 49Those who died in the plague were 14,700, not counting those who died because of Korah.

Aaron stands between the dead and the living

50Then Aaron went back to Moses at the entrance to the tent of meeting, for the plague had been stopped.
fields.summary: Korah, Dathan and Abiram rebel against Moses and Aaron. The ground swallows the rebels, and fire consumes the 250 men offering incense.

fields.title: Numbers 17
fields.body_html:
Aaron’s staff sprouts

1The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 2“Speak to the Israelites and get a staff from them for each ancestral family, one from each of their leaders by their ancestral families: twelve staffs. Write each man’s name on his staff. 3On Levi’s staff you are to write Aaron’s name, because each head of an ancestral family has one staff. 4Then place them in the tent of meeting in front of the testimony, where I meet with you. 5The man I choose is the one whose staff will sprout. So I will make the grumbling of the Israelites against you die down, and it will trouble me no more.” 6So Moses spoke to the Israelites, and all their leaders gave him staffs, one for each leader, by their ancestral families: twelve staffs. Aaron’s staff was among them. 7Moses placed the staffs before the LORD in the tent of the testimony. 8The next day Moses went into the tent of the testimony, and there was Aaron’s staff, the staff for the house of Levi, sprouting. It had put out buds, opened into blossoms, and borne ripe almonds. 9Then Moses brought all the staffs out from before the LORD to all the Israelites. They looked at them, and each leader took back his own staff.

10The LORD said to Moses, “Return Aaron’s staff to its place before the testimony. It is to be kept there as a sign for the rebels, so that you can stop their complaints against me and they do not die.” 11Moses did this. He did just as the LORD had commanded him.

Whoever comes near the tabernacle dies

12Then the Israelites said to Moses, “We are dying! We are perishing, every one of us perishing! 13Whoever comes near, anyone who comes near the tabernacle of the LORD, dies. Will we all perish to the last one?”
fields.summary: The rebels’ censers are hammered into a covering for the altar. When the people grumble again, Aaron stands between the dead and the living to stop the plague, and Aaron’s staff sprouts as a sign.

fields.title: Numbers 18
fields.body_html:
The duties of priests and Levites

1The LORD said to Aaron, “You and your sons and your father’s family with you will bear the guilt for any offense against the sanctuary, and you and your sons with you will bear the guilt for any offense in your priesthood. 2Bring with you also your relatives, the tribe of Levi, your ancestral tribe, so that they may join you and assist you while you and your sons with you are in front of the tent of the testimony. 3They are to carry out their duties to you and their duties for the whole tent, but they must not come near the holy furnishings or the altar, or both they and you will die. 4They are to join you and carry out the duties of the tent of meeting, all the work of the tent, and no outsider may come near you. 5You are to carry out the duties of the sanctuary and the duties of the altar, so that wrath will not fall again on the Israelites. 6I myself have taken your relatives the Levites from among the Israelites. They are a gift to you, given to the LORD, to do the work of the tent of meeting. 7But you and your sons with you are to carry out your priesthood in everything to do with the altar and with what is behind the curtain, and you are to do that service. I am giving you your priesthood as a gift for service. Any outsider who comes near is to be put to death.”

The priests’ portion of the holy gifts

8The LORD spoke to Aaron: “I myself have put you in charge of the contributions made to me, all the holy gifts of the Israelites. I have given them to you and your sons as your portion, a permanent share. 9This is what will be yours from the most holy things, the part not burned in the fire: every offering they bring, whether grain offering, sin offering or guilt offering that they pay back to me. It is most holy, for you and your sons. 10You are to eat it in a most holy place. Every male may eat it. It is to be holy to you. 11This also is yours: the contribution from their gifts, together with all the wave offerings of the Israelites. I have given them to you and to your sons and daughters with you as a permanent share. Everyone in your household who is clean may eat it. 12I have given you all the best of the olive oil and all the best of the new wine and the grain, the first part of the harvest that they give to the LORD. 13The first ripe fruits of everything in their land that they bring to the LORD will be yours. Everyone in your household who is clean may eat them. 14Every devoted thing in Israel will be yours. 15Every firstborn of every living thing that they bring to the LORD, whether human or animal, will be yours. But you must redeem every firstborn human, and you are to redeem the firstborn of unclean animals. 16You are to redeem them from a month old at the set value of about 2 ounces of silver, by the sanctuary standard. 17But you must not redeem the firstborn of a cow, a sheep or a goat; they are holy. Splash their blood against the altar and turn their fat into smoke as a food offering, a soothing aroma to the LORD. 18Their meat will be yours, just as the breast of the wave offering and the right thigh are yours. 19All the holy contributions that the Israelites set aside for the LORD I have given to you and to your sons and daughters with you as a permanent share. It is a covenant of salt forever before the LORD, for you and your descendants with you.” 20The LORD said to Aaron, “You will have no inheritance in their land, and you will have no portion among them. I am your portion and your inheritance among the Israelites.

The tithe for the Levites

21To the Levites I have given every tithe in Israel as their inheritance, in return for the work they do, the work of the tent of meeting. 22The Israelites must no longer come near the tent of meeting, or they will bear the guilt of sin and die. 23It is the Levites who are to do the work of the tent of meeting, and they will bear their guilt. This is a statute for all time, through all your generations. They will have no inheritance among the Israelites. 24For I have given the Levites as their inheritance the tithe that the Israelites set aside as a contribution to the LORD. That is why I have said of them, ‘They will have no inheritance among the Israelites.’”

A tithe of the tithe

25The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 26“Speak to the Levites and tell them: ‘When you receive from the Israelites the tithe that I have given you from them as your inheritance, you are to present a contribution from it to the LORD, a tenth of the tithe. 27Your contribution will be counted for you as if it were grain from the threshing floor or the full yield of the winepress. 28In this way you also are to present a contribution to the LORD from all the tithes you receive from the Israelites. From them you are to give the contribution for the LORD to Aaron the priest. 29From all the gifts you receive you are to present every contribution due to the LORD, taking the best of it as the part to be made holy.’ 30Say to them: ‘When you have presented the best of it, the rest will be counted for the Levites as produce from the threshing floor and from the winepress. 31You and your households may eat it anywhere, for it is your payment in return for your work at the tent of meeting. 32Once you have presented the best of it, you will not bear guilt because of it. But you must not profane the holy gifts of the Israelites, or you will die.’”
fields.summary: The duties of priests and Levites are set out. The priests receive a portion of the holy gifts, the Levites receive the tithe, and they give a tithe of the tithe.

fields.title: Numbers 19
fields.body_html:
The red heifer and the water for cleansing

1The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said, 2“This is the statute of the law that the LORD has commanded: Tell the Israelites to bring you a red heifer that is perfect, with no defect, and that has never been under a yoke. 3You are to give it to Eleazar the priest. It is to be brought outside the camp and slaughtered in his presence. 4Eleazar the priest is to take some of its blood on his finger and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the tent of meeting. 5The heifer is to be burned in his sight. Its hide, its flesh and its blood are to be burned along with its dung. 6The priest is to take cedar wood, hyssop and scarlet yarn and throw them into the fire that is burning the heifer. 7Then the priest must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. After that he may come into the camp, but he will remain unclean until evening. 8The one who burns it must also wash his clothes in water and bathe his body in water, and he too will be unclean until evening. 9A man who is clean is to gather up the ashes of the heifer and put them in a clean place outside the camp. They are to be kept for the congregation of the Israelites, for the water to remove impurity. It is a sin offering. 10The one who gathers up the ashes of the heifer must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening. This is to be a lasting statute for the Israelites and for the outsider who lives among them. 11Whoever touches the dead body of any human being will be unclean for seven days. 12They must purify themselves with the water on the third day and on the seventh day, and then they will be clean. But if they do not purify themselves on the third day and the seventh day, they will not be clean. 13Anyone who touches a dead body, the body of someone who has died, and does not purify themselves makes the tabernacle of the LORD unclean, and that person must be cut off from Israel. The water to remove impurity was not sprinkled on them, so they remain unclean; their uncleanness is still on them. 14This is the law when someone dies in a tent: everyone who enters the tent and everyone who is in it will be unclean for seven days. 15Any open container that has no lid tied down on it is unclean. 16Anyone out in the open field who touches someone killed by the sword, or someone who has died, or a human bone, or a grave, will be unclean for seven days. 17For the unclean person, some of the ashes of the burned sin offering are to be taken and put in a container, and fresh water is to be poured on them. 18Then a man who is clean is to take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle the tent, all its furnishings and the people who were there. He is also to sprinkle anyone who touched a bone, or someone killed, or someone who died, or a grave. 19The clean man is to sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day, and on the seventh day he will have purified them. Then the one being cleansed must wash their clothes and bathe in water, and at evening they will be clean. 20But anyone who is unclean and does not purify themselves must be cut off from among the assembly, because they have made the sanctuary of the LORD unclean. The water to remove impurity has not been sprinkled on them; they are unclean. 21This is to be a lasting statute for them. The one who sprinkles the water to remove impurity must wash his clothes, and anyone who touches that water will be unclean until evening. 22Anything the unclean person touches becomes unclean, and anyone who touches it will be unclean until evening.”
fields.summary: A red heifer is burned to make water for cleansing those who touch a dead body.

fields.title: Numbers 20
fields.body_html:
Water from the rock at Meribah

1In the first month the Israelites, the whole congregation, arrived in the wilderness of Zin, and the people settled at Kadesh. Miriam died there, and there she was buried. 2There was no water for the congregation, and they gathered together against Moses and Aaron. 3The people argued with Moses. “We wish we had died,” they said, “when our brothers and sisters perished before the LORD! 4Why have you brought the assembly of the LORD into this wilderness, for us and our animals to die here? 5Why did you bring us up out of Egypt only to lead us into this terrible place? Nothing can be sown here, and there are no figs, no vines, no pomegranates, and there is not even water to drink!” 6Moses and Aaron left the assembly and went to the entrance of the tent of meeting. They fell face down, and the glory of the LORD appeared to them.

7Then the LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 8“Take the staff, and gather the congregation together, you and your brother Aaron. Then, while they watch, speak to the rock, and it will pour out its water. So you will bring water out of the rock for them and give the congregation and their animals something to drink.” 9So Moses took the staff from its place before the LORD, as he had commanded him. 10Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly in front of the rock, and Moses said to them, “Listen, you rebels! Are we to bring water out of this rock for you?” 11Then Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff. Water gushed out in abundance, and the congregation and their animals drank.

Moses and Aaron will not lead the people in

12But the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “You did not trust me, and so you failed to show my holiness before the Israelites. For that reason you will not be the ones to lead this assembly into the land I have given them.” 13These were the waters of Meribah, “quarreling,” where the Israelites quarreled with the LORD, and he showed himself holy among them.

Edom refuses Israel passage

14From Kadesh Moses sent messengers to the king of Edom: “This is what your brother Israel says: You know about all the hardships we have been through. 15Our ancestors went down to Egypt, and we lived there a long time. The Egyptians mistreated us and our ancestors. 16When we cried out to the LORD, he heard our voice. He sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt. Now we are here at Kadesh, a town on the edge of your territory. 17Allow us, please, to cross your land. We will stay out of your fields and vineyards, and we will not drink from your wells. We will keep to the King’s Highway, turning neither right nor left, until we are out of your territory.” 18But Edom answered, “You will not cross our land. If you try, we will march out against you with the sword.” 19The Israelites replied, “We will go up by the highway, and if we or our herds drink your water, we will pay its price. It is a small thing; all we ask is to cross on foot.” 20But Edom said, “You will not pass through.” And Edom came out against them with a large army and a strong force. 21So Edom refused to let Israel pass through its territory, and Israel turned away from them.

The death of Aaron

22They set out from Kadesh, and the Israelites, the whole congregation, came to Mount Hor. 23At Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom, the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, 24“Aaron is about to be gathered to his people. He will not enter the land I have given to the Israelites, because you both rebelled against my command at the waters of Meribah. 25Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up Mount Hor. 26Remove Aaron’s garments and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron will be gathered to his people and die there.” 27Moses did as the LORD commanded. They climbed Mount Hor in full view of the whole congregation. 28Moses removed Aaron’s garments and put them on his son Eleazar, and Aaron died there on the mountaintop. Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain. 29When the whole congregation saw that Aaron had died, all the house of Israel mourned for him thirty days.
fields.summary: Miriam dies, and at Meribah Moses strikes the rock instead of speaking to it, so he and Aaron will not lead the people into the land. Edom refuses Israel passage, and Aaron dies on Mount Hor.

fields.title: Numbers 21
fields.body_html:
Victory at Hormah

1When the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming along the Atharim road, he attacked Israel and took some of them prisoner. 2Then Israel made a vow to the LORD: “If you will truly hand this people over to us, we will devote their towns to destruction.” 3The LORD listened to Israel’s plea and handed the Canaanites over, and Israel devoted them and their towns to destruction. So the place was named Hormah.

The bronze snake

4They set out from Mount Hor along the road to the Red Sea, to go around the land of Edom, and on the way the people lost patience. 5The people spoke against God and against Moses: “Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? There is no food and no water, and we are sick of this pitiful food!” 6Then the LORD sent fiery snakes among the people. They bit the people, and many Israelites died. 7The people came to Moses and said, “We sinned when we spoke against the LORD and against you. Pray to the LORD to take the snakes away from us.” So Moses prayed for the people. 8The LORD said to Moses, “Make a fiery snake and put it up on a pole. Anyone who is bitten can look at it and live.” 9So Moses made a bronze snake and set it on the pole. Whenever a snake had bitten someone, and that person looked at the bronze snake, they lived. 10The Israelites moved on and camped at Oboth. 11They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, in the wilderness that faces Moab on the east. 12From there they moved on and camped in the Zered Valley. 13From there they moved on and camped on the far side of the Arnon, in the wilderness that reaches out from the Amorite border. The Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.
14That is why it is said in the Book of the Wars of the LORD:
“Waheb in Suphah,
and the valleys of the Arnon,
15and the slope of the valleys
that stretches toward the town of Ar
and lies along the border of Moab.”
16From there they went on to Beer. That is the well where the LORD said to Moses, “Gather the people together, and I will give them water.”

The song of the well

17Then Israel sang this song:
“Spring up, well! Sing out to it!
18the well that princes dug, that the nobles of the people dug out
with a scepter and with their staffs.”
From the wilderness they went on to Mattanah,
19from Mattanah to Nahaliel, from Nahaliel to Bamoth, 20and from Bamoth to the valley in the country of Moab, by the top of Pisgah, which looks down over the wasteland of Jeshimon.

Victory over Sihon and Og

21Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites with this message: 22“Let us pass through your land. We will not turn off into any field or vineyard, and we will not drink water from any well. We will keep to the King’s Highway until we have passed through your territory.” 23But Sihon would not let Israel pass through his territory. He gathered all his forces and marched out into the wilderness against Israel. When he reached Jahaz, he fought against Israel. 24Israel defeated him in battle and took possession of his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the Ammonites, for the Ammonite border was strongly held. 25Israel took all these towns and settled in all the towns of the Amorites, in Heshbon and all its villages. 26Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites. He had fought against the former king of Moab and taken all his land from him, as far as the Arnon.
27That is why the poets say, “Come to Heshbon!
Let the city of Sihon be rebuilt and made strong again!
28For fire went out from Heshbon,
a flame from the city of Sihon.
It burned up Ar of Moab,
the lords of the heights of the Arnon.
29How terrible for you, Moab!
You are destroyed, people of Chemosh!
He has let his sons become refugees and his daughters captives
of Sihon king of the Amorites.
30But we shot at them; Heshbon is destroyed as far as Dibon.
We laid the land waste as far as Nophah,
which reaches to Medeba.”
31So Israel settled in the land of the Amorites. 32Moses sent men to scout out Jazer, and they captured its villages and drove out the Amorites who lived there. 33Then they turned and went up along the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan marched out against them with all his army to fight at Edrei. 34The LORD said to Moses, “Do not be afraid of him, for I have handed him over to you, with all his army and his land. Do to him what you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon.” 35So they struck down Og, his sons and all his army, until not one survivor was left, and they took possession of his land.
fields.summary: Israel defeats the Canaanites at Hormah. When the people complain, fiery snakes bite them, and Moses makes a bronze snake that heals those who look at it; Israel defeats Sihon and Og.

fields.title: Numbers 22
fields.body_html:
Israel camps in the plains of Moab

1Then the Israelites moved on and camped in the plains of Moab, across the Jordan from Jericho.

Balak sends for Balaam

2Balak son of Zippor saw everything that Israel had done to the Amorites. 3Moab was terrified of the people, because there were so many of them; Moab felt a sickening dread of the Israelites. 4So Moab said to the elders of Midian, “Now this assembly will lick up everything around us, as an ox crops the grass of a field.” Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time. 5He sent messengers to call Balaam son of Beor at Pethor, near the River, in the land of his own people. The message said, “A people has come out of Egypt. They are covering the face of the land, and they have settled right across from me. 6So come now, please, and curse this people for me, because they are too strong for me. Perhaps then we will be able to defeat them, and I can drive them out of the land. For I know this: those you bless are blessed, and those you curse are cursed.” 7So the elders of Moab and of Midian set out, carrying the payment for divination. They came to Balaam and gave him Balak’s message. 8Balaam told them, “Stay here tonight. I will bring you a reply, just as the LORD tells it to me.” So the officials of Moab stayed with Balaam. 9God came to Balaam and asked, “Who are these men staying with you?” 10Balaam answered God, “Balak son of Zippor, the king of Moab, has sent me this message, 11‘The people that came out of Egypt are covering the face of the land. Come now and put a curse on them for me. Perhaps then I will be able to fight against them and drive them out.’” 12But God said to Balaam, “You are not to go with them, nor are you to curse the people, because they are blessed.” 13In the morning Balaam got up and said to Balak’s officials, “Go back to your own country. The LORD will not allow me to go with you.” 14So the officials of Moab set off, went back to Balak, and told him, “Balaam will not come with us.” 15Balak sent officials once more, more of them than before, and of higher rank than the first. 16They came to Balaam and said to him, “This is what Balak son of Zippor says: ‘Please let nothing keep you from coming to me, 17for I will give you great honor and do whatever you ask of me. Come, please, and put a curse on this people for me.’” 18Balaam replied to Balak’s officials, “Balak could give me his house filled with silver and gold, and still I could not do anything, small or great, that goes past what the LORD my God has said. 19Now you too, please, stay here tonight, so that I may learn what more the LORD has to say to me.” 20God came to Balaam that night and said to him, “If the men have come to call you, then get up and go with them. But the word I give you, that and only that, you must do.” 21So in the morning Balaam got up, saddled his donkey, and set off with the officials of Moab. 22God’s anger blazed up because Balaam was going, and the angel of the LORD placed himself in the road to stand against him. Balaam was riding his donkey, with two of his servants beside him. 23The donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road, his sword drawn and in his hand, and she left the road and went out into the field. Balaam struck her to bring her back to the road. 24Next the angel of the LORD took his place where the path ran narrow among the vineyards, walled in on this side and on that. 25The donkey saw the angel of the LORD and pushed herself up against the wall, squeezing Balaam’s foot against it, and he struck her once more. 26Once more the angel of the LORD went on ahead. This time he stood in a tight spot with no way around him, right or left. 27The donkey saw the angel of the LORD and sank down under Balaam. Then Balaam’s anger flared, and he struck the donkey with his staff. 28Then the LORD opened the donkey’s mouth, and she said to Balaam, “What wrong have I done you, that you have struck me these three times?” 29Balaam said to the donkey, “Because you have made me look a fool! If there were a sword in my hand, you would be dead already.” 30The donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not your own donkey? You have ridden me all your life, up to this very day. Was it ever my way to treat you like this?” “No,” he answered. 31Then the LORD opened Balaam’s eyes. Now he could see the angel of the LORD standing in the road, his sword drawn and in his hand, and Balaam bowed his head and threw himself down, face to the ground. 32The angel of the LORD said to him, “Why have you struck your donkey these three times? It was I who came out to stand against you, because the way you are going is reckless in my sight. 33Three times the donkey saw me and swerved away from me. Had she not swerved away, I would have killed you by now, and kept her alive.” 34Balaam said to the angel of the LORD, “I have sinned. I did not know you were there in the road, standing to face me. Now, if this displeases you, I will turn back.” 35The angel of the LORD said to Balaam, “Go on with the men. But the word I give you, that and only that, you are to speak.” So Balaam went on with Balak’s officials. 36News reached Balak that Balaam was on his way, and he went out to meet him at the city of Moab, which stands on the Arnon border at the very edge of the territory. 37Balak said to Balaam, “I sent for you with such urgency! Why did you not come to me? Did you think I could not pay you what you are worth?” 38Balaam replied, “Here I am; I have come to you. But can I say just anything now? The word God places in my mouth, that is what I will speak.” 39Then Balaam went with Balak, and they came to Kiriath-huzoth. 40Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and sent some of the meat to Balaam and to the officials who were with him. 41The next morning Balak took Balaam and brought him up to Bamoth-baal. From there Balaam could see the outer edge of the people.
fields.summary: Israel camps in the plains of Moab, and King Balak sends for Balaam to curse them. On the way Balaam’s donkey sees an angel and speaks.

fields.title: Numbers 23
fields.body_html:
Balaam’s first and second oracles

1Balaam said to Balak, “Build me seven altars here, and get seven bulls and seven rams ready for me here.” 2Balak did as Balaam said, and Balak and Balaam offered a bull and a ram on each altar. 3Then Balaam said to Balak, “Stay here beside your burnt offering while I go. Perhaps the LORD will come to meet me. Whatever he shows me, I will tell you.” And he went off to a bare hill. 4God met Balaam, and Balaam said to him, “I have set up the seven altars, and on each altar I have offered a bull and a ram.” 5The LORD put a message in Balaam’s mouth and said, “Go back to Balak and say this.” 6So he went back to Balak and found him standing beside his burnt offering with all the officials of Moab.
7Then Balaam spoke his oracle:
“Balak, king of Moab, brought me from Aram, from the mountains of the east:
‘Come, curse Jacob for me;
come, condemn Israel.’
8How can I curse a people God has not cursed?
How can I condemn a people the LORD has not condemned?
9From the tops of the rocks I see them;
from the hills I watch them.
Here is a people that lives apart
and does not count itself as one of the nations.
10Who can count the dust of Jacob
or number even a fourth of Israel?
Let me die the death of the upright,
and may my end be like theirs!”
11Balak said to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I brought you here to curse my enemies, and instead you have done nothing but bless them!” 12Balaam answered, “Do I not have to be careful to say what the LORD puts in my mouth?” 13Then Balak said to him, “Please come with me to another place where you can see them. You will see only the outer edge of them, not all of them. Curse them for me from there.” 14So he took him to the field of Zophim on the top of Pisgah. There he built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar. 15Balaam said to Balak, “Stay here beside your burnt offering while I go over there to meet with God.” 16The LORD met Balaam, put a message in his mouth, and said, “Go back to Balak and say this.” 17So he came to Balak and found him standing beside his burnt offering with the officials of Moab. Balak asked him, “What did the LORD say?”
18Then Balaam spoke his oracle:
“Rise, Balak, and listen;
hear me, son of Zippor.
19God is not a human, who might lie,
nor a mortal, who might change course.
Would he say something and not do it?
Would he speak and not make it happen?
20Look, I was given orders to bless;
he has blessed, and I cannot reverse it.
21He sees no disaster for Jacob
and no trouble for Israel.
The LORD their God is with them,
and the shout for a king rings out among them.
22God brought them out of Egypt;
they have strength like the horns of a wild ox.
23No omen can work against Jacob,
no divination against Israel.
Now it will be said of Jacob and of Israel,
‘See what God has done!’
24Here is a people that rises up like a lioness
and rouses itself like a lion.
It does not lie down until it has eaten its prey
and drunk the blood of the slain.”
25Then Balak said to Balaam, “Do not curse them at all, and do not bless them at all!” 26Balaam answered Balak, “Did I not tell you that I must do whatever the LORD says?” 27Then Balak said to Balaam, “Come, please, let me take you to another place. Perhaps it will please God to let you curse them for me from there.” 28So Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, which overlooks the Jeshimon. 29Balaam said to Balak, “Build me seven altars here, and get seven bulls and seven rams ready for me here.” 30Balak did as Balaam said, and he offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
fields.summary: Balaam blesses Israel instead of cursing them in his first and second oracles.

fields.title: Numbers 24
fields.body_html:
Balaam’s last oracles

1When Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he did not go off to look for omens as he had done the other times. Instead he turned his face toward the wilderness. 2Balaam looked up and saw Israel camped tribe by tribe, and the Spirit of God came upon him.
3Then he spoke his oracle:
“These are the words of Balaam son of Beor,
the words of the man whose eye is opened,
4the words of one who hears what God says,
who sees the vision of the Almighty,
who falls to the ground with eyes wide open:
5How fine your tents are, Jacob,
your dwellings, Israel!
6They are like stream valleys reaching far,
like gardens by a river,
like aloes that the LORD has planted,
like cedars beside the water.
7Water will flow from his buckets,
and his seed will have abundant water.
His king will be greater than Agag,
and his kingdom will be lifted high.
8God brings him out of Egypt;
his strength is like the horns of a wild ox.
He will devour the nations that are his enemies, crush their bones and strike them with his arrows.
9He crouches and lies down like a lion, like a lioness: who dares to rouse him?
Blessed are those who bless you,
and cursed are those who curse you!”
10Balak was furious with Balaam. He struck his hands together and said to Balaam, “I called you here to curse my enemies, and instead you have done nothing but bless them, three times now. 11Now get out of here and go home! I said I would reward you with great honor, but the LORD has kept you from any honor.” 12Balaam answered Balak, “Did I not tell the messengers you sent to me, 13‘Even if Balak gave me his house filled with silver and gold, I could not go beyond the command of the LORD to do anything good or bad of my own will. What the LORD says, that is what I will say’? 14So now I am going back to my people. But come, let me tell you what this people will do to your people in the days to come.”
15Then he spoke his oracle:
“These are the words of Balaam son of Beor,
the words of the man whose eye is opened,
16the words of one who hears what God says
and has knowledge from the Most High,
who sees the vision of the Almighty,
who falls to the ground with eyes wide open:
17I see him, but not now;
I look on him, but he is not near.
A star will march out of Jacob, and a scepter will rise from Israel;
he will crush the forehead of Moab
and tear down all the people of Sheth.
18Edom will become his possession; Seir, his enemies, will become his possession,
while Israel does mighty deeds.
19One from Jacob will rule,
and he will wipe out the survivors of the city.”
20Then he looked at Amalek and spoke his oracle:
“Amalek was first among the nations,
but in the end it will perish completely.”
21Then he looked at the Kenites and spoke his oracle:
“Your home is secure,
and your nest is set in the rock,
22yet Kain will be burned up.
How long until Asshur carries you away captive?”
23Then he spoke his oracle again:
“Alas, who can survive when God does this?
24Ships will come from the coast of Kittim;
they will bring down Asshur and bring down Eber,
but he too will perish completely.”
25Then Balaam got up and went back home, and Balak also went on his way.
fields.summary: Balaam blesses Israel again and foretells a star rising from Jacob.

fields.title: Numbers 25
fields.body_html:
Israel binds itself to the Baal of Peor

1Israel settled at Shittim, and there the people began to commit sexual immorality with the women of Moab. 2These women invited the people to the sacrifices for their gods, and the people ate and bowed down to their gods. 3So Israel bound itself to the Baal of Peor, and the anger of the LORD burned against Israel. 4The LORD said to Moses, “Take all the leaders of the people and impale them before the LORD in the light of day, so that the burning anger of the LORD will leave Israel.” 5So Moses said to the judges of Israel, “Each of you is to kill the men under his authority who have bound themselves to the Baal of Peor.” 6Just then one of the Israelites came and brought a Midianite woman to his relatives. He did it in full view of Moses and the whole congregation of the Israelites, as they wept at the entrance of the tent of meeting. 7When Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he stood up from among the congregation and seized a spear. 8He went after the Israelite man into the inner tent and ran the spear through both of them, the Israelite man and the woman, through her belly. And the plague that was striking the Israelites came to a stop. 9The number who died in the plague was 24,000.

A covenant of peace for Phinehas

10Then the LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 11“Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned my wrath away from the Israelites, because he burned with my zeal among them. So I did not wipe out the Israelites in my zeal. 12Therefore say: ‘I now give him my covenant of peace. 13It will be for him and for his descendants after him a covenant of priesthood for all time, because he showed zeal for his God and made atonement for the Israelites.’” 14The Israelite man killed along with the Midianite woman was named Zimri son of Salu; he was a leader of an ancestral family of the Simeonites. 15The Midianite woman who was killed was called Cozbi daughter of Zur. Zur was head of the clans of an ancestral family in Midian.

Be hostile to the Midianites

16Then the LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 17“Be hostile to the Midianites and strike them down. 18For they are hostile to you with the tricks they played on you in the affair of Peor and in the affair of Cozbi, their kinswoman, the daughter of a leader of Midian, who was killed on the day of the plague that came because of Peor.”
fields.summary: Israel binds itself to the Baal of Peor, and a plague breaks out. Phinehas stops it and is given a covenant of peace, and Israel is told to be hostile to the Midianites.

fields.title: Numbers 26
fields.body_html:
The second census

1After the plague, the LORD said to Moses and to Eleazar son of Aaron, the priest, 2“Take a census of the whole congregation of the Israelites by their ancestral families, all the men in Israel twenty years old and up, everyone who can go out to war.” 3So Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke with the people on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho. They said, 4“Count the men twenty years old and up,” as the LORD had commanded Moses. These were the Israelites who came out of the land of Egypt: 5Reuben was Israel’s firstborn. The descendants of Reuben were: from Hanoch, the clan of the Hanochites; from Pallu, the clan of the Palluites; 6from Hezron, the clan of the Hezronites; and from Carmi, the clan of the Carmites. 7These were the clans of the Reubenites. The number enrolled from them was 43,730. 8The son of Pallu was Eliab. 9The sons of Eliab were Nemuel, Dathan and Abiram. These are the same Dathan and Abiram, men chosen from the congregation, who fought against Moses and Aaron with Korah’s company when they fought against the LORD. 10The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them along with Korah, when his company died and the fire devoured 250 men. They became a warning. 11But the sons of Korah did not die.

12The descendants of Simeon by their clans: from Nemuel, the clan of the Nemuelites; from Jamin, the clan of the Jaminites; from Jachin, the clan of the Jachinites; 13from Zerah, the clan of the Zerahites; and from Shaul, the clan of the Shaulites. 14These were the clans of the Simeonites, 22,200 in number.

15The descendants of Gad by their clans: from Zephon, the clan of the Zephonites; from Haggi, the clan of the Haggites; from Shuni, the clan of the Shunites; 16from Ozni, the clan of the Oznites; from Eri, the clan of the Erites; 17from Arod, the clan of the Arodites; and from Areli, the clan of the Arelites. 18These were the clans of the descendants of Gad. The number enrolled from them was 40,500.

19The sons of Judah included Er and Onan, but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. 20The descendants of Judah by their clans were: from Shelah, the clan of the Shelanites; from Perez, the clan of the Perezites; and from Zerah, the clan of the Zerahites. 21The descendants of Perez were: from Hezron, the clan of the Hezronites; and from Hamul, the clan of the Hamulites. 22These were the clans of Judah. The number enrolled from them was 76,500.

23The descendants of Issachar by their clans: from Tola, the clan of the Tolaites; from Puvah, the clan of the Punites; 24from Jashub, the clan of the Jashubites; and from Shimron, the clan of the Shimronites. 25These were the clans of Issachar. The number enrolled from them was 64,300.

26The descendants of Zebulun by their clans: from Sered, the clan of the Seredites; from Elon, the clan of the Elonites; and from Jahleel, the clan of the Jahleelites. 27These were the clans of the Zebulunites. The number enrolled from them was 60,500.

28The descendants of Joseph by their clans were Manasseh and Ephraim. 29The descendants of Manasseh were: from Machir, the clan of the Machirites (Machir was the father of Gilead); from Gilead, the clan of the Gileadites. 30These were the descendants of Gilead: from Iezer, the clan of the Iezerites; from Helek, the clan of the Helekites; 31from Asriel, the clan of the Asrielites; from Shechem, the clan of the Shechemites; 32from Shemida, the clan of the Shemidaites; and from Hepher, the clan of the Hepherites. 33Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons, only daughters. The names of Zelophehad’s daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah. 34These were the clans of Manasseh. The number enrolled from them was 52,700.

35These were the descendants of Ephraim by their clans: from Shuthelah, the clan of the Shuthelahites; from Becher, the clan of the Becherites; and from Tahan, the clan of the Tahanites. 36These were the descendants of Shuthelah: from Eran, the clan of the Eranites. 37These were the clans of the descendants of Ephraim. The number enrolled from them was 32,500. These were the descendants of Joseph by their clans.

38The descendants of Benjamin by their clans: from Bela, the clan of the Belaites; from Ashbel, the clan of the Ashbelites; from Ahiram, the clan of the Ahiramites; 39from Shephupham, the clan of the Shuphamites; and from Hupham, the clan of the Huphamites. 40The sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman: from Ard, the clan of the Ardites; and from Naaman, the clan of the Naamites. 41These were the descendants of Benjamin by their clans. The number enrolled from them was 45,600.

42These were the descendants of Dan by their clans: from Shuham, the clan of the Shuhamites. These were the clans of Dan, clan by clan. 43The number enrolled from all the clans of the Shuhamites was 64,400.

44The descendants of Asher by their clans: from Imnah, the clan of the Imnites; from Ishvi, the clan of the Ishvites; and from Beriah, the clan of the Beriites. 45From the descendants of Beriah: from Heber, the clan of the Heberites; and from Malchiel, the clan of the Malchielites. 46Asher’s daughter was named Serah. 47These were the clans of the descendants of Asher. The number enrolled from them was 53,400.

48The descendants of Naphtali by their clans: from Jahzeel, the clan of the Jahzeelites; from Guni, the clan of the Gunites; 49from Jezer, the clan of the Jezerites; and from Shillem, the clan of the Shillemites. 50These were the clans of Naphtali. The number enrolled from them was 45,400. 51The total number of the Israelites enrolled was 601,730.

Dividing the land by lot

52Then the LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 53“The land is to be divided among these as their inheritance, according to the number of names. 54To a large tribe you are to give a larger inheritance, and to a small tribe a smaller one. Each is to be given its inheritance according to the number of those enrolled in it. 55But the land is to be divided by lot. They are to receive their inheritance by the names of their ancestral tribes. 56Each inheritance is to be divided by lot between the larger and the smaller tribes.”

The census of the Levites

57These were the Levites enrolled by their clans: from Gershon, the clan of the Gershonites; from Kohath, the clan of the Kohathites; and from Merari, the clan of the Merarites. 58These were the clans of Levi: the clan of the Libnites, the clan of the Hebronites, the clan of the Mahlites, the clan of the Mushites and the clan of the Korahites. Kohath was the father of Amram. 59Amram’s wife was named Jochebed. She was a daughter of Levi, born to Levi in Egypt. To Amram she bore Aaron, Moses and their sister Miriam. 60Aaron became the father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. 61But Nadab and Abihu died when they offered an improper fire before the LORD. 62The Levites enrolled numbered 23,000, every male one month old and up. They were not enrolled with the other Israelites, because they were given no inheritance among them. 63These are the ones enrolled by Moses and Eleazar the priest when they enrolled the Israelites on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho. 64Among them there was not one man of those enrolled by Moses and Aaron the priest when they enrolled the Israelites in the wilderness of Sinai. 65For the LORD had said of them, “They will certainly die in the wilderness.” Not one of them was left except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
fields.summary: Moses and Eleazar take a second census of the new generation, and the land is to be divided by lot. The Levites are counted, and none of the first generation is left except Caleb and Joshua.

fields.title: Numbers 27
fields.body_html:
The daughters of Zelophehad

1Then the daughters of Zelophehad came forward. Zelophehad was the son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, and belonged to the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph. His daughters were named Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah. 2They stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders and the whole congregation at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and said, 3“Our father died in the wilderness. He was not one of the company who banded together against the LORD, the company of Korah. He died for his own sin, and he had no sons. 4Why should our father’s name disappear from his clan because he had no son? Give us property among our father’s brothers.” 5So Moses brought their case before the LORD.

6The LORD said to Moses, 7“The daughters of Zelophehad are right in what they say. You must give them a property as an inheritance among their father’s brothers, and transfer their father’s inheritance to them. 8And tell the Israelites, ‘If a man dies and has no son, you are to transfer his inheritance to his daughter. 9If he has no daughter, you are to give his inheritance to his brothers. 10If he has no brothers, you are to give his inheritance to his father’s brothers. 11If his father has no brothers, you are to give his inheritance to the nearest relative in his clan, and he will take possession of it. This is to be a legal statute for the Israelites,’” just as the LORD commanded Moses.

Joshua appointed to succeed Moses

12Then the LORD said to Moses, “Climb this mountain in the Abarim range and look out over the land I have given to the Israelites. 13When you have seen it, you too will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was, 14for when the congregation quarreled in the wilderness of Zin, you rebelled against my command to show my holiness before their eyes at the waters.” (These were the waters of Meribah at Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin.)

15Moses said to the LORD, 16“May the LORD, the God of the spirits of all humankind, appoint a man over the congregation, 17someone who will go out ahead of them and come in ahead of them, who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the congregation of the LORD will not be like sheep with no shepherd.” 18So the LORD said to Moses, “Take Joshua son of Nun, a man with the spirit in him, and lay your hand on him, 19have him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation, and commission him in their sight, 20and give him some of your authority, so that the whole congregation of the Israelites will obey him. 21He is to stand before Eleazar the priest, who will seek decisions for him before the LORD by means of the Urim. At his word they will go out, and at his word they will come in, Joshua and all the Israelites with him, the whole congregation.” 22Moses did as the LORD had commanded him. He took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation, 23and he laid his hands on him and commissioned him, as the LORD had directed through Moses.
fields.summary: The daughters of Zelophehad ask to inherit their father’s land, and God grants it. Moses sees the land from a mountain, and Joshua is appointed to succeed him.

fields.title: Numbers 28
fields.body_html:
The daily offerings

1The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 2“Command the Israelites and tell them: ‘Be careful to present to me at its appointed time my offering, my food, given as my food offerings, a soothing aroma to me.’ 3Tell them: ‘Each day you are to present to the LORD, as a food offering, two year-old male lambs without defect. This is the regular burnt offering. 4One lamb is to be offered in the morning, and the other as evening comes on. 5The grain offering for each lamb is to be about 2 quarts of fine flour mixed with about a quart of pressed olive oil. 6It is the regular burnt offering, as it was offered at Mount Sinai: a soothing aroma, a food offering to the LORD. 7Its drink offering is to be about a quart for each lamb. In the holy place pour out the drink offering of strong drink to the LORD. 8The second lamb you are to offer as evening comes on, with a grain offering and a drink offering like those of the morning: a food offering, a soothing aroma to the LORD.

Sabbath offerings

9On the Sabbath day there are to be two year-old male lambs without defect, with about 4 quarts of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and its drink offering, 10as the burnt offering of each Sabbath, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.

Offerings at the start of each month

11Each month, on its first day, you are to bring the LORD a burnt offering: two young bulls, one ram and seven male lambs in their first year, every one of them without defect. 12The grain offering for each bull is to be about 6 quarts of fine flour mixed with oil, and for the ram about 4 quarts of fine flour mixed with oil, 13and for each lamb about 2 quarts of fine flour mixed with oil. This is a burnt offering, a soothing aroma, a food offering to the LORD. 14The wine for their drink offerings is to be about 2 quarts with each bull, about 1 1/4 quarts with the ram and about a quart with each lamb. This is the burnt offering for the new moon, month after month through the year. 15Also one male goat is to be offered to the LORD as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.

Passover and the Festival of Unleavened Bread

16In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, the Passover is kept for the LORD. 17A festival is held on the fifteenth day of this month, and for seven days the bread eaten is to be made without yeast. 18The first day is to be a holy assembly, when you do none of your ordinary work. 19You are to bring the LORD a food offering, a burnt offering made up of two young bulls, one ram and seven male lambs in their first year. See that they are without defect. 20With them offer a grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: about 6 quarts for each bull and about 4 quarts for the ram. 21For each of the seven lambs offer about 2 quarts. 22Also offer one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you. 23All this is to be offered besides the morning burnt offering, which belongs to the regular burnt offering. 24Offer this food each day for seven days as a food offering, a soothing aroma to the LORD. It is added to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering. 25The seventh day is to be a holy assembly for you, when you do none of your ordinary work.

The day of firstfruits

26The day of firstfruits, when you bring the LORD a grain offering from the new crop at your Festival of Weeks, is to be a holy assembly for you. Do none of your ordinary work. 27You are to present a burnt offering, a soothing aroma to the LORD, of two young bulls, one ram and seven year-old male lambs, 28with their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: about 6 quarts for each bull, about 4 quarts for the ram, 29and about 2 quarts for each of the seven lambs, 30and one male goat to make atonement for you. 31Bring all these besides the regular burnt offering and its grain offering, and their drink offerings with them. The animals must be without defect.
fields.summary: God sets out the offerings for each day, each Sabbath, the start of each month, Passover and the Festival of Unleavened Bread, and the day of firstfruits.

fields.title: Numbers 29
fields.body_html:
The day of trumpet blasts

1On the first day of the seventh month you are to hold a holy assembly and do none of your ordinary work. It is a day for you when loud blasts are sounded. 2Offer a burnt offering as a soothing aroma for the LORD: one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, without defect. 3Their grain offering is to be fine flour mixed with oil: about 6 quarts for the bull, about 4 quarts for the ram, 4and about 2 quarts for each of the seven lambs. 5Offer also one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you, 6in addition to the burnt offering of the new moon with its grain offering, and the regular burnt offering with its grain offering, and their drink offerings, as prescribed for them. They are a soothing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.

The tenth day of the seventh month

7On the tenth day of this seventh month you are to hold a holy assembly. Humble yourselves by fasting, and do no work of any kind. 8Present to the LORD a burnt offering as a soothing aroma: one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old. See that they are all without defect. 9Their grain offering is to be fine flour mixed with oil: about 6 quarts for the bull, about 4 quarts for the ram, 10and about 2 quarts for each of the seven lambs. 11Offer also one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the sin offering for atonement, and the regular burnt offering with its grain offering, and their drink offerings.

The seven-day festival of the seventh month

12On the fifteenth day of the seventh month you are to hold a holy assembly and do none of your ordinary work. Celebrate a festival for the LORD for seven days. 13Present a burnt offering, a food offering with a soothing aroma for the LORD: thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old. They are to be without defect. 14Their grain offering is to be fine flour mixed with oil: about 6 quarts for each of the thirteen bulls, about 4 quarts for each of the two rams, 15and about 2 quarts for each of the fourteen lambs. 16Offer also one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and its drink offering.

17On the second day offer twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, without defect, 18with their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed, 19and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

20On the third day offer eleven young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, without defect, 21with their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed, 22and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

23On the fourth day offer ten young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, without defect, 24with their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed, 25and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

26On the fifth day offer nine young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, without defect, 27with their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed, 28and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
