29On the sixth day offer eight young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, without defect, 30with their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed, 31and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

32On the seventh day offer seven young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, without defect, 33with their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed, 34and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.

The eighth day

35The eighth day is to be a solemn assembly for you, and you are to do none of your ordinary work. 36Present a burnt offering, a food offering with a soothing aroma for the LORD: one bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, without defect, 37with their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bull, the ram and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed, 38and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering. 39These are the offerings you are to bring to the LORD at your appointed festivals, in addition to your vow offerings and your freewill offerings, whether burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings or peace offerings.’” 40So Moses told the Israelites everything the LORD had commanded him.
fields.summary: God sets out the offerings for the day of trumpet blasts, the tenth day of the seventh month and the seven-day festival with its eighth day.

fields.title: Numbers 30
fields.body_html:
Vows and pledges

1Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes of the Israelites. He said, “This is what the LORD has commanded: 2When a man makes a vow to the LORD or swears an oath that binds him to a pledge, he must not break his word. He must do everything he has said. 3When a woman makes a vow to the LORD or binds herself by a pledge while she is young and still living in her father’s house, 4and her father hears of her vow or her pledge and says nothing to her, then all her vows stand, and every pledge by which she has bound herself stands. 5But if her father forbids her on the day he hears of it, none of her vows or pledges by which she has bound herself will stand. The LORD will forgive her, because her father has forbidden her. 6If she marries while she is still under her vows, or under a rash promise of her lips by which she has bound herself, 7and her husband hears of it and says nothing to her on the day he hears, then her vows stand, and the pledges by which she has bound herself stand. 8But if her husband forbids her on the day he hears of it, he cancels the vow she is under and the rash promise of her lips by which she has bound herself, and the LORD will forgive her. 9But any vow of a widow or a divorced woman, anything by which she has bound herself, is binding on her. 10If a woman living in her husband’s house makes a vow or binds herself by a pledge with an oath, 11and her husband hears of it and says nothing to her and does not forbid her, then all her vows stand, and every pledge by which she has bound herself stands. 12But if her husband cancels them on the day he hears of them, then nothing that came from her lips, whether vows or pledges binding her, will stand. Her husband has cancelled them, and the LORD will forgive her. 13Any vow or any sworn pledge to deny herself, her husband may confirm or her husband may cancel. 14But if her husband says nothing to her from one day to the next, he confirms all her vows and all the pledges she is under. He has confirmed them, because he said nothing to her on the day he heard of them. 15But if he cancels them later, after the day he heard of them, he will bear the guilt that would have been hers.” 16These are the statutes that the LORD commanded Moses about a man and his wife, and about a father and his daughter while she is young and living in her father’s house.
fields.summary: Rules are given for vows and pledges, and when a father or husband may cancel a woman’s vow.

fields.title: Numbers 31
fields.body_html:
Vengeance on the Midianites

1The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 2“Take vengeance on the Midianites for the Israelites. After that you will be gathered to your people.” 3So Moses said to the people, “Arm some of your men for war, and let them go against Midian to carry out the LORD’s vengeance on Midian. 4Send a thousand men from each of the tribes of Israel to the war.” 5So a thousand from each tribe were provided from the clans of Israel, 12,000 men armed for war. 6Moses sent them to the war, a thousand from each tribe, together with Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, who had in his care the holy articles and the trumpets for sounding the alarm. 7They made war on Midian, as the LORD had commanded Moses, and killed every man. 8Along with the others who were killed, they killed the kings of Midian, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba, the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword. 9The Israelites took the women of Midian and their children captive, and they carried off all their cattle, all their flocks and all their goods as plunder. 10They burned all the towns where the Midianites lived, and all their camps. 11They took all the spoil and all the plunder, both people and animals. 12They brought the captives, the plunder and the spoil to Moses, to Eleazar the priest and to the congregation of the Israelites, at the camp on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho.

Moses is angry with the officers

13Moses, Eleazar the priest and all the leaders of the congregation went out to meet them outside the camp. 14Moses was angry with the officers of the army, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, who were coming back from the battle. 15Moses said to them, “You have let all the women live? 16These are the very women who, on Balaam’s advice, led the Israelites to be unfaithful to the LORD in the affair of Peor, so that the plague struck the congregation of the LORD. 17So now kill every boy among the children, and kill every woman who has slept with a man. 18But keep alive for yourselves all the girls who have not slept with a man. 19As for you, camp outside the camp for seven days. All of you who have killed anyone or touched anyone killed must purify yourselves and your captives on the third day and on the seventh day. 20Purify also every garment, everything made of leather or of goat hair, and every object of wood.”

Cleansing after the battle

21Then Eleazar the priest said to the soldiers who had gone into battle, “This is the statute of the law that the LORD commanded Moses: 22Only the gold, the silver, the bronze, the iron, the tin and the lead, 23everything that can stand fire, you are to put through fire, and it will be clean. But it must also be purified with the water for impurity. Whatever cannot stand fire you are to put through the water. 24On the seventh day wash your clothes, and you will be clean. After that you may come into the camp.”

Dividing the plunder

25The LORD said to Moses, 26“You and Eleazar the priest and the heads of the families of the congregation are to count the plunder that was captured, both people and animals. 27Divide the plunder into two halves, one for the men who fought in the battle and went out to war, and one for the whole congregation. 28From the men who fought and went out to war, set apart a tribute for the LORD: one out of every 500, whether people, cattle, donkeys or sheep. 29Take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as a contribution for the LORD. 30And from the half that belongs to the Israelites take one out of every fifty, whether people, cattle, donkeys or sheep, from all the animals, and give them to the Levites who carry out the duties of the LORD’s tabernacle.” 31So Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the LORD had commanded Moses. 32The plunder, what was left of the spoil the soldiers had taken, came to 675,000 sheep, 3372,000 cattle, 3461,000 donkeys, 35and 32,000 people in all, girls who had not slept with a man. 36The half that was the share of those who had gone out to war came to 337,500 sheep, 37and the tribute for the LORD from the sheep was 675. 38There were 36,000 cattle, and the tribute from them for the LORD was seventy-two. 39There were 30,500 donkeys, and the tribute from them for the LORD was sixty-one. 40There were 16,000 people, and the tribute from them for the LORD was thirty-two people. 41Moses gave the tribute, the LORD’s contribution, to Eleazar the priest, as the LORD had commanded Moses. 42Then there was the half that belonged to the Israelites, which Moses had separated from that of the men who fought. 43The congregation’s half came to 337,500 sheep, 4436,000 cattle, 4530,500 donkeys, 46and 16,000 people. 47From this half that belonged to the Israelites Moses took one out of every fifty, of people and of animals, and gave them to the Levites who carry out the duties of the LORD’s tabernacle, as the LORD had commanded Moses. 48Then the officers over the units of the army, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, came to Moses 49and said to him, “Your servants have counted the soldiers under our command, and not one man of us is missing. 50So we have brought as an offering to the LORD what each man found, articles of gold: armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings and necklaces, to make atonement for ourselves before the LORD.” 51Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from them, all of it crafted jewelry. 52All the gold that the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds presented as a contribution to the LORD weighed about 420 pounds. 53Each of the soldiers had taken plunder for himself. 54Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from the commanders of thousands and of hundreds and brought it into the tent of meeting as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD.
fields.summary: Israel takes vengeance on the Midianites, and Moses is angry that the officers spared the women. The soldiers are cleansed, and the plunder is divided.

fields.title: Numbers 32
fields.body_html:
Reuben and Gad ask for land east of the Jordan

1The Reubenites and the Gadites owned a great deal of livestock, a very large number of animals. They saw that the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead was just the place for livestock. 2So the Gadites and the Reubenites came and spoke to Moses, to Eleazar the priest and to the leaders of the congregation. They said, 3“Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo and Beon, 4the land that the LORD conquered for the congregation of Israel, is a land for livestock, and your servants have livestock.”

5“If we have found favor with you,” they said, “let this land be given to your servants as their property. Do not make us cross the Jordan.” 6Moses said to the Gadites and the Reubenites, “Are your brothers to go to war while you stay here? 7Why would you discourage the Israelites from crossing over into the land that the LORD has given them? 8That is what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to look over the land. 9They went up as far as the Valley of Eshcol and saw the land, and then they discouraged the Israelites from entering the land that the LORD had given them. 10The LORD’s anger burned on that day, and he swore this oath: 11‘Not one of the men who came up out of Egypt, twenty years old and over, will see the land I swore to give to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, because they have not followed me with all their heart, 12except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun, for they have followed the LORD with all their heart.’ 13The LORD’s anger burned against Israel, and he made them wander in the wilderness for forty years, until the whole generation that had done what was evil in the sight of the LORD had died out. 14And now you have taken your fathers’ place, a new generation of sinners, to make the anger of the LORD burn against Israel even more! 15If you turn away from following him, he will once again leave this people in the wilderness, and you will bring ruin on them all.”

An agreement with Reuben and Gad

16Then they came up to him and said, “We will build pens here for our livestock and towns for our little ones, 17But we ourselves will arm for battle and go eagerly ahead of the Israelites until we have brought them to their place. Meanwhile our little ones will live in fortified towns, safe from the people of the land. 18We will not go back to our homes until every one of the Israelites has received an inheritance. 19We will not take an inheritance with them on the far side of the Jordan and beyond, because our inheritance has come to us on this side of the Jordan, to the east.”

20Moses answered them, “If you do this, if you arm yourselves for battle before the LORD, 21and every armed man among you crosses the Jordan before the LORD until he has driven out his enemies before him, 22and the land is brought under control before the LORD, then afterward you may return. You will be free of your duty to the LORD and to Israel, and this land will be your property before the LORD. 23But if you do not do this, then you will have sinned against the LORD, and you can be sure that your sin will catch up with you. 24Build towns for your little ones and pens for your flocks, but do what you have promised.” 25The Gadites and the Reubenites said to Moses, “Your servants will do just as my lord commands. 26Our little ones, our wives, our livestock and all our other animals will stay there in the towns of Gilead, 27but your servants, every man armed for war, will cross over before the LORD to the battle, as my lord says.” 28So Moses gave orders about them to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun, and to the heads of the ancestral families of the tribes of the Israelites. 29Moses said to them, “If the Gadites and the Reubenites cross the Jordan with you before the LORD, every man armed for battle, and the land is brought under control before you, then give them the land of Gilead as their property. 30But if they do not cross over with you armed, they are to receive their property among you in the land of Canaan.” 31The Gadites and the Reubenites answered, “Your servants will do what the LORD has said. 32We will cross over armed before the LORD into the land of Canaan, but the property we inherit will be ours on this side of the Jordan.” 33So Moses gave to the Gadites, the Reubenites and half the tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan: the land with its towns and their territories, the towns of the whole region. 34The Gadites built Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer, 35Atroth-shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah, 36Beth-nimrah and Beth-haran, as fortified towns, and they built pens for their flocks. 37The Reubenites built Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim, 38Nebo and Baal-meon (their names were changed), and Sibmah. They gave new names to the towns they built. 39The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead, captured it and drove out the Amorites who lived there. 40So Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he settled there. 41Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, went and captured their villages, and he named them Havvoth-jair. 42And Nobah went and captured Kenath and its villages, and he named it Nobah after himself.
fields.summary: Reuben and Gad ask for land east of the Jordan for their livestock. Moses agrees on the condition that their men cross over and fight with the other tribes.

fields.title: Numbers 33
fields.body_html:
The stages of Israel’s journey from Egypt

1These are the stages of the journey of the Israelites when they came out of the land of Egypt by their divisions, led by Moses and Aaron. 2Moses wrote down the places they set out from, stage by stage, at the LORD’s command. These are their journeys, listed by their starting points. 3They set out from Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month. On the day after the Passover the Israelites marched out boldly in full view of all the Egyptians, 4while the Egyptians were burying all their firstborn, whom the LORD had struck down among them. The LORD had also carried out judgments on their gods. 5The Israelites set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth. 6They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness. 7They set out from Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, which faces Baal-zephon, and they camped in front of Migdol. 8They set out from Pi-hahiroth and went through the middle of the sea into the wilderness. After three days’ travel in the wilderness of Etham, they camped at Marah. 9They set out from Marah and came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there. 10They set out from Elim and camped by the Red Sea. 11They set out from the Red Sea and camped in the wilderness of Sin. 12They set out from the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah. 13They set out from Dophkah and camped at Alush. 14They set out from Alush and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink. 15They set out from Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai. 16They set out from the wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah. 17They set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth. 18They set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah. 19They set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez. 20They set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah. 21They set out from Libnah and camped at Rissah. 22They set out from Rissah and camped at Kehelathah. 23They set out from Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher. 24They set out from Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah. 25They set out from Haradah and camped at Makheloth. 26They set out from Makheloth and camped at Tahath. 27They set out from Tahath and camped at Terah. 28They set out from Terah and camped at Mithkah. 29They set out from Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah. 30They set out from Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth. 31They set out from Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan. 32They set out from Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad. 33They set out from Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah. 34They set out from Jotbathah and camped at Abronah. 35They set out from Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber. 36They set out from Ezion-geber and camped in the wilderness of Zin, that is, at Kadesh. 37They set out from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, on the edge of the land of Edom. 38Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor at the LORD’s command, and he died there on the first day of the fifth month, in the fortieth year after the Israelites came out of the land of Egypt. 39Aaron was 123 years old when he died on Mount Hor.

40The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev in the land of Canaan, heard that the Israelites were coming. 41They set out from Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah. 42They set out from Zalmonah and camped at Punon. 43They set out from Punon and camped at Oboth. 44They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, on the border of Moab. 45They set out from Iye-abarim and camped at Dibon-gad. 46They set out from Dibon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim. 47They set out from Almon-diblathaim and camped in the Abarim mountains, facing Nebo. 48They set out from the Abarim mountains and camped in the plains of Moab beside the Jordan, across from Jericho. 49Their camp stretched along the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim in the plains of Moab.

Drive out the people of the land

50The LORD spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab beside the Jordan, across from Jericho. He said, 51“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: ‘When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan, 52drive out all the people who live in the land ahead of you. Destroy all their carved stones, destroy all their cast metal idols, and tear down all their high places. 53Take possession of the land and settle in it, for I have given the land to you to possess. 54Divide the land among yourselves as an inheritance by lot, clan by clan. Give a larger inheritance to a larger clan and a smaller inheritance to a smaller one. Wherever the lot falls for a clan, that place will be its own. You are to receive your inheritance by your ancestral tribes. 55But if you do not drive out the people who live in the land ahead of you, those you allow to stay will be like splinters in your eyes and thorns in your sides. They will make trouble for you in the land where you live. 56And then I will do to you what I planned to do to them.’”
fields.summary: The stages of Israel’s journey from Egypt to the plains of Moab are listed. Israel must drive out the people of the land and destroy their idols.

fields.title: Numbers 34
fields.body_html:
The borders of the land of Canaan

1The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 2“Give the Israelites this command and tell them: ‘You are about to enter the land of Canaan. Here is the land that will fall to you as your inheritance, the land of Canaan with these borders: 3Your southern side will take in the wilderness of Zin, alongside Edom. On the east, your southern border will start at the end of the Dead Sea. 4From there your border will turn and run south of the Ascent of Akrabbim and on to Zin, reaching as far as the south of Kadesh-barnea. Then it will go out to Hazar-addar and on to Azmon. 5From Azmon the border will bend around to the Wadi of Egypt and end at the sea. 6Your western border will be the Great Sea and its coast. That will be your border on the west. 7This will be your northern border: from the Great Sea mark out a line to Mount Hor. 8From Mount Hor mark it out to Lebo-hamath, and the border will reach out to Zedad. 9The border will continue to Ziphron and end at Hazar-enan. This will be your northern border. 10For your eastern border, mark out a line from Hazar-enan to Shepham. 11From Shepham the border will go down to Riblah, on the east side of Ain, and on down until it meets the slopes east of the Sea of Chinnereth. 12Then the border will go down along the Jordan and end at the Dead Sea. This will be your land, with its borders on every side.’” 13Moses gave the Israelites this command: “This is the land you are to divide among yourselves by lot as your inheritance. The LORD has commanded that it be given to the nine tribes and the half-tribe. 14For the tribe of the Reubenites and the tribe of the Gadites, by their ancestral families, have already received their inheritance, and so has the half-tribe of Manasseh. 15These two tribes and the half-tribe have received their inheritance across the Jordan from Jericho, on the east, toward the sunrise.”

The men who are to divide the land

16The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 17“These are the names of the men who are to divide the land among you as your inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun. 18You are also to take one leader from every tribe to divide up the land. 19These are the names of the men: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh, 20from the tribe of Simeon, Shemuel son of Ammihud, 21from the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon, 22from the tribe of Dan, the leader Bukki son of Jogli, 23from the descendants of Joseph: from the tribe of Manasseh, the leader Hanniel son of Ephod, 24from the tribe of Ephraim, the leader Kemuel son of Shiphtan, 25from the tribe of Zebulun, the leader Elizaphan son of Parnach, 26from the tribe of Issachar, the leader Paltiel son of Azzan, 27from the tribe of Asher, the leader Ahihud son of Shelomi, 28and from the tribe of Naphtali, the leader Pedahel son of Ammihud.” 29These are the men whom the LORD commanded to divide the inheritance among the Israelites in the land of Canaan.
fields.summary: God sets the borders of the land of Canaan and names the men who are to divide it.

fields.title: Numbers 35
fields.body_html:
Cities for the Levites

1The LORD spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho. He said, 2“Command the Israelites to give the Levites cities to live in, out of the land they will hold as their inheritance. Give the Levites pastureland around the cities as well. 3They will live in the cities and use the pasturelands for their cattle, their livestock and all their other animals. 4The pastureland of the cities you give to the Levites is to reach out from the city wall about 1,500 feet in every direction. 5Measure outside the city about 3,000 feet on the east side, about 3,000 feet on the south side, about 3,000 feet on the west side and about 3,000 feet on the north side, with the city in the middle. This will be the pastureland of their cities. 6Among the cities you give the Levites are to be the six cities of refuge, which you are to provide so that anyone who has killed someone can flee there. In addition to these, give them forty-two other cities. 7In all, you are to give the Levites forty-eight cities, together with their pasturelands. 8The cities you give from the land the Israelites hold are to be taken in proportion: more from a large tribe and fewer from a small one. Each tribe is to give some of its cities to the Levites according to the size of the inheritance it receives.”

Cities of refuge

9The LORD spoke to Moses. He said, 10“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: ‘When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan, 11choose cities to be your cities of refuge, so that anyone who kills a person by mistake can flee there. 12The cities will be a refuge for you from the avenger, so that one who has killed someone does not die before standing trial before the congregation. 13You are to provide six cities in all as cities of refuge. 14Provide three cities across the Jordan and three in the land of Canaan. They are to be cities of refuge. 15These six cities will be a refuge for the Israelites and for the foreigners and temporary residents who live among them, so that anyone who kills a person by mistake can flee there. 16But if someone strikes another person with an iron object and that person dies, the one who struck is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death. 17If someone strikes another person with a stone in the hand that could kill, and that person dies, the one who struck is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death. 18Or if someone strikes another person with a wooden object in the hand that could kill, and that person dies, the one who struck is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death. 19It is the avenger of blood who is to put the murderer to death, wherever he finds them. 20If anyone shoves someone out of hatred, or lies in wait and throws something at that person, and the person dies, 21or strikes someone with the hand out of hostility, and the person dies, the one who struck must be put to death as a murderer. The avenger of blood is to put the murderer to death wherever he finds them. 22But if anyone pushes someone suddenly, without hostility, or throws any object at that person without lying in wait, 23or drops a stone heavy enough to kill on someone without seeing that person, and the person dies, even though there was no enmity between them and no wish to do harm, 24then the congregation is to judge between the one who struck and the avenger of blood according to these rulings. 25The congregation is to protect the one who killed from the avenger of blood and return that person to the city of refuge where they fled. The one who killed must live there until the death of the high priest, who was anointed with the holy oil. 26But if the one who killed ever goes outside the boundary of the city of refuge where they fled, 27and the avenger of blood finds them outside the boundary of that city of refuge and kills them, the avenger is not guilty of bloodshed. 28For the one who killed must stay in the city of refuge until the high priest dies. After the death of the high priest, they may go back to their own land. 29These are to be a legal statute for you throughout your generations, wherever you live. 30When someone is accused of killing a person, the murderer may be put to death only if witnesses testify to it. The word of one witness is not enough to put anyone to death. 31Do not accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who is guilty and deserves to die. Such a murderer must be put to death. 32Nor are you to accept a ransom for one who has fled to a city of refuge, to let them go back and live on their own land before the priest dies. 33Do not pollute the land where you live. Bloodshed pollutes the land, and when blood has been shed on it, nothing can make atonement for the land except the blood of the one who shed it. 34Do not make unclean the land where you live, the land where I dwell, for I, the LORD, dwell among the Israelites.’”
fields.summary: Forty-eight towns are given to the Levites, six of them cities of refuge for anyone who kills a person by accident.

fields.title: Numbers 36
fields.body_html:
The inheritance of daughters who marry

1Then the heads of the families in the clan of Gilead’s descendants came forward. Gilead was the son of Machir, son of Manasseh, and belonged to the clans of Joseph’s descendants. They spoke before Moses and the leaders, the heads of the ancestral families of the Israelites. 2They said, “The LORD commanded you, my lord, to give the land to the Israelites as an inheritance by lot, and you, my lord, were commanded by the LORD to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters. 3But if they become the wives of men from one of the other tribes of the Israelites, their inheritance will be taken away from the inheritance of our ancestors and added to the inheritance of the tribe they will then belong to. So it will be taken away from the share that fell to us by lot. 4And when the Jubilee of the Israelites arrives, their inheritance will be joined to the inheritance of the tribe they then belong to, and the inheritance of our ancestral tribe will lose it.” 5Then Moses gave the Israelites this command at the word of the LORD: “The tribe of Joseph’s descendants is right in what it says. 6This is what the LORD commands for the daughters of Zelophehad: ‘They are free to marry the man they prefer, as long as he is from a clan of their father’s tribe. 7An inheritance of the Israelites must not change hands from tribe to tribe, for each of the Israelites is to hold fast to the inheritance of their ancestral tribe. 8Any daughter who comes into an inheritance in one of the tribes of the Israelites is to become the wife of a man from a clan of her father’s tribe. In this way each of the Israelites will keep possession of their ancestors’ inheritance. 9An inheritance must not change hands from one tribe to another, for each tribe of the Israelites is to hold fast to its own inheritance.’” 10The daughters of Zelophehad did just as the LORD had commanded Moses. 11Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, married the sons of their uncles. 12It was into clans descended from Manasseh son of Joseph that they married, so their inheritance stayed with the tribe of their father’s clan. 13These are the commandments and rulings that the LORD gave the Israelites through Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho.
fields.summary: Daughters who inherit land must marry within their tribe so that tribal land stays in the tribe.

fields.title: Conclusion
fields.body_html:
These are the commandments and rulings that the LORD gave the Israelites through Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho.

— Numbers 36:13

Numbers ends where it has been heading for forty years: on the plains of Moab, by the Jordan, across from Jericho. The land is in sight. But almost everyone who set out from Sinai is gone. Miriam is buried at Kadesh and Aaron on Mount Hor, and Moses has been told that he will see the land only from a mountain. The people camped by the river are their children, counted, organised and ready, waiting to cross.

The question the book leaves with you

Why did a whole generation, who had seen the sea split and eaten bread from heaven, never reach the land? Numbers answers plainly, and so does the New Testament when it looks back: “So we see that it was unbelief that kept them from entering.” They believed the giants more than the promise. They remembered Egypt’s cucumbers and forgot its whips. And when the moment came, they would not go.

That is the question Numbers puts to every reader. Not whether God is faithful, because the book shows that again and again: the manna every morning, the cloud every night, the pardon at Moses’ prayer, the blessing that Balaam could not turn into a curse. The question is whether we will trust him at the border. Caleb is the book’s answer, the man with “another spirit in him”, who “followed me with all his heart”. And behind Caleb stands a God who keeps his word to the children even when the parents have failed.

Where the story goes next

The next book, Deuteronomy, is Moses’ farewell to this new generation, spoken on these same plains. After it, Joshua will lead them across the Jordan. But the wilderness was never only a place. The prophets remembered it as the time of Israel’s first love, and the psalmists as a warning. And the New Testament finds the whole book retold in Jesus.

The Spirit led him into the wilderness for forty days, where he was tempted as Israel had been, and he answered each temptation with words Moses spoke to the wilderness generation. He called himself the true manna: “Your ancestors ate the manna in the wilderness, and yet they died”, but “I am the living bread, come down from heaven.” He said that he would be lifted up as the bronze snake was lifted up. And Paul tells the Corinthians that the rock that gave water in the desert was Christ, and that the whole story was told for us:

“What happened to them was meant as an example, and it was written down to warn us, who live at the time when the ages reach their end.”

— 1 Corinthians 10:11

The letter to the Hebrews draws the same lesson and adds the hope: “So a Sabbath rest is still waiting for God’s people.” The wilderness is not the end of the road.

Where to go from here

Numbers has been a favourite of preachers, who have found the pilgrim church on every page. A few places to begin in this library:

  • On the whole book. Hannah Whitall Smith’s Old Testament Types and Teachings, whose chapter “Numbers: Wilderness Wanderings” reads the wanderings as a picture of the Christian who has been redeemed but has not yet entered into the fulness of salvation.
  • On the cloud and the voice (Numbers 7–9). Alexander Maclaren’s The Guiding Pillar (Numbers 9:16); and Andrew Murray’s The Inner Chamber, whose chapter “Moses and the Word of God” turns on Numbers 7:89, Moses hearing the voice from above the mercy seat.
  • On the scouts and Caleb (Numbers 13–14). Gareth Evans’s Caleb: A Different Spirit (Numbers 14:24).
  • On the tassels and the priests’ portion (Numbers 15 and 18). Hudson Taylor’s A Ribband of Blue (Numbers 15:38–39); and A. W. Tozer’s God’s Best Is Himself (Numbers 18:20).
  • On the rock in the wilderness (Numbers 20). Christmas Evans’s The Smitten Rock, on 1 Corinthians 10:4, which dwells on Moses striking the rock twice.
  • On Balaam (Numbers 22–24). Horatius Bonar’s The Vain Wish, on Balaam’s prayer to die the death of the upright (Numbers 23:10).
  • On Phinehas and the priesthood (Numbers 25). Andrew Murray’s The Two Covenants, with its chapter “The Covenant of an Everlasting Priesthood”.
  • On the wilderness as a warning and a hope. A. W. Tozer’s The Sin of Murmuring (1 Corinthians 10:1–13); John Wesley’s sermon “The Wilderness State”, in his Sermons on Several Occasions, on the believer who has come out of Egypt but lost his way; R. A. Torrey’s The Day of Golden Opportunity (Hebrews 3:7); and Charles H. Spurgeon’s Heavenly Rest (Hebrews 4:9).

You can also go the other way, from the text to the classics. Every reference to Numbers in this library can be tapped to read the verse, and the Scripture pages gather, chapter by chapter, what the great writers of the church have said about each passage of this book.

And then read on, to the plains of Moab and Moses’ last words. The people waiting by the Jordan have failed and been forgiven, and they go forward under the words that even a hired seer could not keep from saying:

He sees no disaster for Jacob and no trouble for Israel. The LORD their God is with them, and the shout for a king rings out among them.

— Numbers 23:21
